a_rows_sample.anchor: External research provides strong theoretical foundations for epistemic reasoning systems, but does not establish "Epistemic Operating System" as a canonical architecture pattern.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive summary of an external-literature research pass: the term 'Epistemic Operating System' does not exist as an established academic concept; three core subsystems are identified as required for epistemically robust reasoning -- belief management, contradiction detection, truth constraint enforcement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A truth maintenance system (TMS) is the collection of procedures and data structures used for accomplishing belief revision. ... no belief is kept without a reason.
a_rows_sample.statement: Truth Maintenance System (TMS) definition and core task cited from external research (Martins & Shapiro 1991): maintain conclusions such that (1) not known contradictory, (2) no belief kept without a reason. Two approaches: single-context (JTMS/LTMS) vs multiple-context (ATMS/MBR).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expansion (K + phi) / Contraction (K - phi) / Revision (K * phi) ... AGM Postulates for Revision (K*1-K*8)
a_rows_sample.statement: AGM (Alchourron, Gardenfors, Makinson) belief revision theory cited: three basic operations (Expansion, Contraction, Revision) and the eight AGM postulates K*1..K*8 for revision, plus the semantic interpretation 'AGM revision equivalent to total preorders'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic logic with justification, along with the usual knowledge operator, contains assertions t:F (t is a justification for F). ... Knowledge is true justified belief (Plato)
a_rows_sample.statement: Justification logic (Artemov 2004) cited: extends epistemic logic with explicit justification terms t:F; distinguishes Ki-phi (agent i knows phi, justified true belief) from Bi-phi (agent i believes phi, may be false/unjustified); extends to multi-agent distributed/common knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Structured belief base B_t with accompanying justification graph ... Immutable evidence E* as external reference for validation ... Cryptographically verifiable ledger for epistemic history ... Minimal-mutilation principles for revision
a_rows_sample.statement: Recent (June 2025) 'Structuring Epistemic Integrity in Artificial Reasoning Systems' framework cited: requires evidentialist constraints, Bayesian updating, logical closure schemas; components include structured belief base B_t, immutable evidence E*, dependency-directed backtracking, cryptographically verifiable ledger, minimal-mutilation revision principles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Belief Management | Contradiction Detection | Truth Constraint Enforcement | Justification Tracking | Provenance Management | Revision Protocol
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Epistemic Operating System architecture: six core subsystems (Belief Management, Contradiction Detection, Truth Constraint Enforcement, Justification Tracking, Provenance Management, Revision Protocol) plus data structures (structured belief base B_t, justification graph DAG, immutable evidence E*, epistemic ledger, cognitive worlds) and five invariants (epistemic consistency, justificatory transparency, minimal mutilation, global acyclicity, truth preservation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No established "Epistemic OS" pattern: The term is emerging, not canonical ... Limited integration with organizational governance ... Human-AI epistemic collaboration ... Temporal epistemic logic
a_rows_sample.statement: Six identified research gaps: no established Epistemic-OS pattern; limited integration with organizational governance; TMS/RMS scalability challenges; limited probabilistic/symbolic integration; limited human-AI epistemic collaboration research; limited bi-temporal epistemic logic research.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EPI-001: Justification Transparency. Draft: Every belief must have an explicit, auditable justification graph. Evaluation: Strongly supported. Classification: Strong candidate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Five candidate invariants for an Epistemic Operating System, each tested against cited research and classified: EPI-001 Justification Transparency (strong candidate), EPI-002 Epistemic Consistency (strong candidate), EPI-003 Minimal Mutilation (candidate), EPI-004 Provenance Homogeneity (research hypothesis), EPI-005 Immutable Evidence Reference (research hypothesis).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No belief is kept without a reason. ... KnowledgeOS must preserve: Decision -> justification -> AI summary -> source document. The chain matters.
a_rows_sample.statement: TMS's 'no belief without a reason' is claimed to strengthen the Transformation Integrity candidate invariant: a Document->AI Summary->Decision chain must preserve the full justification chain back to the source document.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Justification Integrity: Every derived knowledge state SHALL preserve an explicit justification chain. ... 2. Belief/Core Separation ... 3. Revision Integrity ... 4. Provenance Context: Knowledge meaning SHALL include the provenance conditions under which it is valid.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four un-numbered candidate invariants proposed for promotion from the epistemic-OS research review: (1) Justification Integrity (every derived knowledge state SHALL preserve an explicit justification chain, per TMS/RMS/justification logic), (2) Belief/Core Separation (derived conclusions SHALL remain distinguishable from authoritative knowledge, per TMS/RMS), (3) Revision Integrity (knowledge evolution SHALL preserve minimal justified change, per AGM), (4) Provenance Context (knowledge meaning SHALL include the provenance conditions under which it is valid, per provenance-enhanced KGs).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a software platform for constructing, maintaining, investigating, evaluating, and acting upon governed knowledge states.
a_rows_sample.statement: Positions KnowledgeOS as an 'Epistemic Operating System for AI and human engineering', explicitly not primarily a database, knowledge graph, RAG system, LLM, chatbot, agent framework, document-management system, workflow engine or rules engine (though it can use all of these); its product category answers 'how does an intelligent actor operate responsibly on knowledge when knowledge is incomplete, uncertain, conflicting, contextual and continuously changing?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \rightarrow Evaluate \rightarrow Gap/Conflict \rightarrow Investigate \rightarrow K_{t+1}
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS 'operates the knowledge lifecycle' rather than storing knowledge: Intent+Observation+Evidence -> Knowledge State -> Epistemic Navigation -> Decision/Action, iteratively K_t -> Evaluate -> Gap/Conflict -> Investigate -> K_{t+1}. Dimension Discovery is elevated to a first-class capability D_{t+1}=Discover(D_t,Q,O,K_t,C), letting KnowledgeOS operate below the level of explicit user specification — 'the Knower does not need to know the ontology in advance'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS becomes an epistemic substrate for AI agents.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent loop (LLM->Tools->Action) with a KnowledgeOS-enabled agent that queries intent, current knowledge, supporting evidence, unknowns, conflicts, missing dimensions, next investigation, assumptions, Ideal State and discrepancy before acting — positioning KnowledgeOS as 'an epistemic substrate for AI agents', potentially its strongest product position. Also preserves the Observation->Assertion->Evidence->Inference->Hypothesis->Decision provenance chain for traceable reasoning, valuable for engineering/governance/compliance/safety-critical environments, and makes governance executable at the epistemic level (Knowledge->Evidence requirements->Epistemic rules->Validation->Decision eligibility->Action authorization), able to state 'this information exists but is not sufficiently evidenced for this decision'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS \rightarrow \text{better structured epistemic conditions for reasoning and decision}
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit product boundaries: KnowledgeOS does not guarantee Knowledge=Truth, Inference=Truth, or Decision=Correct Decision; it makes uncertainty explicit and governable but cannot eliminate uncertainty from reality — KnowledgeOS -> 'better structured epistemic conditions for reasoning and decision'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Product category\n\nEpistemic Operating System
a_rows_sample.statement: Final positioning: product category = Epistemic Operating System; product function = Knowledge State Management + Epistemic Navigation; enterprise positioning = Governed Knowledge Infrastructure for Humans and AI; AI positioning = Epistemic Runtime for AI Agents; engineering positioning = a system for evidence-backed, inspectable, continuously evolving engineering knowledge. Final loop: Intent->Knowledge State->Epistemic Evaluation->Investigation->Understanding->Decision->Action->Observation->Knowledge State', with Zero=epistemic diagnosis, Lord=epistemic horizon expansion, Sārathi=epistemic navigation, KnowledgeOS=the runtime coordinating the cycle — the point where KnowledgeOS 'stops being merely an AI platform and becomes a genuinely new product concept: an operating system for knowledge and epistemic work'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI models become cognitive engines inside KnowledgeOS; KnowledgeOS becomes the epistemic operating environment in which those engines operate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not replace the LLM but contain it: AI models become cognitive engines inside KnowledgeOS, which becomes the epistemic operating environment; AI Model ⊂ KnowledgeOS rather than KnowledgeOS = AI Model. Supplies a 20-row capability-mapping table translating current AI capabilities (RAG, summarization, classification, planning, tool use, memory, hallucination reduction, uncertainty, conflict handling, auditability, etc.) into KnowledgeOS capabilities (evidence-backed acquisition, knowledge transformation, Sārathi navigation, governed action execution, persistent Knowledge State, evidence/provenance/coherence controls, explicit epistemic state, conflict model, provenance+state history).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Level 1 — KnowledgeOS + external AI
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a three-level maturity roadmap: Level 1 KnowledgeOS + external AI (single external model, 'most realistic first implementation'); Level 2 KnowledgeOS + multiple models (model-agnostic, hosting OpenAI/Anthropic/local models simultaneously, KnowledgeOS 'governs how their outputs become knowledge'); Level 3 KnowledgeOS + own foundation models ('a complete independent AI platform').

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI Capability \neq Epistemic Governance
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes as a fundamental architectural invariant: AI Capability ≠ Epistemic Governance, and KnowledgeOS = AI Capability + Knowledge State + Epistemic State + Evidence + Context + Governance + Navigation (provided AI capabilities are supplied by component models). KnowledgeOS's distinctive value is not generating better text than an LLM but providing 'the epistemic machinery around intelligence' — what the system knows, does not know, why it believes something, what conflicts, what is missing, what else might matter, whether it is justified in acting — which is why 'Epistemic Operating System' is kept as the product identity rather than 'another AI platform'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Foundation models are trained on large datasets. OpenAI describes three broad sources for its models: 1. publicly available information, 2. information obtained through third-party partnerships, 3. information provided or generated by users, human trainers, and researchers.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cites OpenAI's own description of ChatGPT's information sources: (A) training-time learned parameters from public data, third-party partnerships, and user/trainer/researcher-provided data — the model is 'a learning machine, not a document database'; (B) inference-time retrieval (ChatGPT Search) that goes beyond built-in training knowledge and provides citations. Concludes mechanism (B) is much closer to what KnowledgeOS needs than (A).

Introduces a KnowledgeOS 'Source Plane' distinct from the 'Knowledge Plane', both feeding an Epistemic Engine (Zero/Lord/Sārathi): Source Plane answers 'where did this information come from?' (documents, APIs, git); Knowledge Plane answers 'what do we currently represent as knowledge?' (entities, assertions, dimensions, relations); Epistemic Engine answers 'how justified, complete, current and coherent is that knowledge?'. Proposes Source Connectors (file system, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, Markdown, Git, GitLab, GitHub, Confluence, SharePoint, Jira, Databases, REST APIs, Web, Email, enterprise repositories) as a first-class platform capability that must NOT simply dump content into a vector database but produce a controlled ingestion event.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a constitutional memory and reasoning system that protects the relationship between the Knower, the Known, and the Path of Reasoning through time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a two-tier final definition: a first-pass definition ('KnowledgeOS is an epistemic reasoning substrate that preserves, evaluates, evolves, and governs the conditions required for trustworthy knowledge discovery') and a deeper restatement (the anchor); framed as a refinement of prior definitions from earlier documents (e.g. S0226's 'constitutional epistemic type system' definition).

b_rows_sample.anchor: I know why I believe what I believe
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates 'What KnowledgeOS Is Not': not a database (databases store facts; KnowledgeOS stores facts+origin+meaning+context+authority+reasoning+history+uncertainty); not a knowledge graph (a graph stores relationships; KnowledgeOS governs whether those relationships are trustworthy); not an AI brain (AI generates hypotheses; KnowledgeOS determines what/why/how-strongly to believe and when to revise); not a truth oracle (does not claim 'I know everything', claims the anchor instead).

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI reasons. KnowledgeOS governs reasoning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates a 'Constitutional Governance' layer from a set of interchangeable 'Reasoning Engines' (LLM, TMS, Logic Solver, Simulation, Human Expert) that feed into 'Knowledge Evolution', stating the anchor as the governing principle of AI's role inside KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a system that stores knowledge. It is a system that preserves the possibility of knowing.
b_rows_sample.statement: States 'The Deepest Character Statement' (the anchor) followed by a 'Final One-Sentence Definition for architecture documentation' ('KnowledgeOS is a constitutional epistemic operating system that enables trustworthy truth discovery by preserving the identity, context, evidence, reasoning, uncertainty, agency, and historical evolution of knowledge across time'), and an Architectural Classification table scoring KnowledgeOS as: Database=No, Knowledge Base=No, AI Agent Framework=No, Knowledge Graph=Partial, Reasoning Engine=Partial, Governance System=Partial, Epistemic Operating System=Yes.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the alias 'Epistemic Operating System'

a_rows_sample.anchor: An enterprise does not have only one uncertainty ... U_1,...,U_n ... resources are finite ... How should KnowledgeOS allocate limited epistemic resources across competing uncertainties and decisions?
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes NextBestEpistemicAction (single decision) to organization-wide resource allocation across many competing uncertainties.

a_rows_sample.anchor: mathcal U={u_1,...,u_n} unresolved knowledge problems ... mathcal R={r_1,...,r_m} available resources ... Allocate(mathcal R,mathcal U) to maximize decision quality
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the central resource-allocation problem Allocate(R,U).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A conventional backlog might assign Priority=High/Medium/Low. That is insufficient ... Cost(U_1)=1 and Cost(U_2)=100. Their resource efficiency differs dramatically
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects simple High/Medium/Low prioritization as insufficient once cost varies dramatically.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(u) as the expected improvement in decision quality resulting from resolving uncertainty u ... Efficiency(u)=EU(u)/Cost(u). But we need more dimensions
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines epistemic utility and a first cost-efficiency ratio, noting it is insufficient alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(u)=f(Risk,DecisionImpact,VOI,Urgency,Dependency,Freshness,Cost). We should resist collapsing these prematurely into one scalar
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a multi-dimensional priority function and warns against premature scalar collapse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Priority=0.83. What does that mean? It hides why the item matters ... Score != Explanation. KnowledgeOS should preserve the underlying vector
a_rows_sample.statement: States a single priority score hides explanatory information, giving the principle Score != Explanation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(u)=(Impact,Risk,VOI,Urgency,Dependency,Freshness,Cost,Authority) ... Only at the optimization boundary may we derive a ranking
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the epistemic priority vector as the preserved, informative representation, deferring scalar ranking to the optimization boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C(d) in {Low,Medium,High,Critical}. This is domain/governance information. KnowledgeOS should not decide what Critical means
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines decision criticality as domain/governance-owned information, not KnowledgeOS-decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Impact(u,d) ... unknown backup restorability may have Impact(u_1,d_migration)=High
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines uncertainty impact on a specific decision, worked with a backup-restorability example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: u_1 -> A -> M -> D_1,D_2,D_3 ... u_1 influences several decisions. This gives Centrality(u_1) high value
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines dependency centrality of an uncertainty influencing multiple decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Degree(u), Betweenness(u), Reachability(u) ... graph-theoretic indicators. But they are not automatically epistemic importance. A highly connected irrelevant node can still be irrelevant
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that raw graph-theoretic centrality measures are not automatically epistemic importance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DWC(u) = sum_d Criticality(d)*Impact(u,d). This is a conceptual formulation
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes decision-weighted centrality combining decision criticality and per-decision impact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Urgency(u,t) ... Deadline(d)-t may approach zero. Then the value of resolving u can increase sharply
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines urgency as a time-dependent factor that can sharply increase resolution value near a deadline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Freshness(u,t) ... InfrastructureState decays quickly ... ArchitecturalPrinciple decays slowly. freshness is domain-specific
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines knowledge freshness as domain-specific, contrasting fast-decaying infrastructure state with slow-decaying architectural principles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HL(u) as the characteristic time over which knowledge becomes stale ... useful for scheduling revalidation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a conceptual knowledge half-life for scheduling revalidation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicDebt is accumulated unresolved uncertainty that can impair future decisions ... undocumented infrastructure; stale architecture decisions; unverified assumptions; unresolved conflicting requirements; missing provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Epistemic Debt as accumulated unresolved uncertainty impairing future decisions, with five worked examples.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Technical debt: ShortTermSpeed->FutureCost. Epistemic debt: UnresolvedUncertainty->FutureDecisionRisk. EpistemicDebt=DeferredKnowledgeWork with future decision consequences
a_rows_sample.statement: Analogizes epistemic debt to technical debt and formalizes it as deferred knowledge work with future decision consequences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D_E(t+1)=D_E(t)+NewUncertainty-ResolvedUncertainty+Staleness. This is conceptual rather than a universal accounting equation
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual debt-accumulation recurrence, explicitly not a universal accounting equation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U_1 remains unresolved. It becomes an assumption in M_1 ... an assumption in D_1. The original uncertainty now propagates. Unresolved uncertainty can compound
a_rows_sample.statement: States unresolved uncertainty can compound as it becomes embedded as an assumption in downstream models and decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Blocker(u) ... u -> D_1,D_2,D_3,D_4, then resolving u may unlock substantial work. This is an epistemic bottleneck
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an epistemic bottleneck as an uncertainty blocking many downstream activities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: When is there enough trustworthy knowledge to make a decision? This is different from asking whether a claim is true. A decision may depend on multiple independently necessary conditions
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the central epistemic-sufficiency question, distinct from claim truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sufficient(K,d) means that the available knowledge satisfies the epistemic conditions required by d. Sufficient(K,d_1) does not imply Sufficient(K,d_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines decision-specific epistemic sufficiency, non-transferable across decisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(SystemHealthy)=0.95. That might be sufficient for LowRiskPlanning. It may be completely insufficient for SafetyCriticalDeployment. EpistemicSufficiency is decision-specific
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example establishing sufficiency is decision-specific, no universal threshold.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pre(d) = {p_1,...,p_n}. Pre(d) = {IdentityConfirmed, CurrentStateKnown, SecurityValidated, GovernanceApproved}. The decision is admissible only if its required preconditions are satisfied
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines decision preconditions with a four-item worked example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If p_1 is necessary: d=>p_1. But satisfying p_1 does not necessarily imply d. Necessary != Sufficient
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally distinguishes necessary from sufficient conditions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SecurityValidated may be necessary. But it is not sufficient. We may also require TestingPassed, ArchitectureApproved, RollbackAvailable
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked production-deployment example of multiple necessary-but-not-individually-sufficient conditions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A,B,C,D are mandatory. Then Sufficient(d) = A and B and C and D. This is the simplest assurance composition
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes conjunctive assurance composition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A=True, B=True, C=False, D=True, then Sufficient=False. It does not matter that 75% of the conditions passed. For mandatory conditions, one missing condition can block the decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked weakest-link counterexample: 75% pass rate is still insufficient given one mandatory failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(A)=0.99, Assurance(B)=0.99, Assurance(C)=0.10. An average gives 0.693. That does not mean 69.3% safe. The low-assurance critical condition may be decisive
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample warning against averaging assurance scores, which masks a decisive low-assurance condition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Criticality(p_i). But we should not simply multiply all probabilities together unless the probabilistic assumptions justify doing so. Mathematical composition requires semantic assumptions
b_rows_sample.statement: States criticality-weighted composition requires justified semantic assumptions, not blind multiplication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance = (Claim, Evidence, Method, Context, Time, Uncertainty, Validation, Scope). The scalar can be derived when appropriate
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines assurance as a structured eight-field object rather than a bare scalar.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceRequirement(d). Decision: Production Deployment. Required: Identity confirmed, Architecture approved, Security validated, Tests passed, Rollback demonstrated, Governance authorized. This is much closer to executable governance
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a worked executable evidence-requirement specification for production deployment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KS(K,d) in {True,False,Unknown}. Because sometimes we cannot establish whether the requirements are satisfied. Unknown must not silently become False or True
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines knowledge sufficiency as a three-valued predicate preventing Unknown from silently collapsing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: mathbb L_3 = {T,F,U}. T=established true; F=established false; U=unknown/undetermined. This is particularly useful for incomplete knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines three-valued epistemic logic L3.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A simplified three-valued conjunction: T/T=T, T/F=F, T/U=U, F/T=F, F/F=F, F/U=F, U/T=U, U/F=F, U/U=U. This is more appropriate than forcing missing knowledge into false
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full three-valued conjunction truth table.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Similarly disjunction: T/T=T, T/F=T, T/U=T, F/T=T, F/F=F, F/U=U, U/T=T, U/F=U, U/U=U. This allows reasoning with incomplete information
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full three-valued disjunction truth table.

b_rows_sample.anchor: IdentityConfirmed=T, SecurityValidated=T, RollbackDemonstrated=U. Then Sufficient=False if rollback is mandatory, or Unknown if the policy itself does not establish whether rollback is mandatory
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example applying three-valued conjunction to a concrete deployment decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gate(d,K). Possible states: Pass, Fail, Blocked, Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a decision gate as a four-state predicate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A gate can pass epistemically while the decision remains unauthorized. GatePass != Authorization. This reinforces Step 40
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes gate-pass from authorization, reinforcing Step 40's authority-vs-truth distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(d) = Compose(A_1,A_2,A_3). But the composition rule must be explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes assurance composition as requiring an explicit composition rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not promote any [EXP] to [THM]
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit recommendation list of what NOT to do next: don't further tune the generator, don't widen the Pi x Q grid, don't declare a 'no-bridge law', don't promote [EXP] to [THM] (a theorem needs a proof not more evidence), don't move to a new algebra/Vedic-derived operator, don't test the Gita strand further for kernel candidacy, and don't open Theory v1.3 before adjudication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every future mathematical statement in KnowledgeOS must carry its epistemic status: Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopted 2026-09-04 for the KnowledgeOS research lane, issued by the human research owner as a permanent methodological rule; an untagged mathematical statement is declared a defect — the exact mechanism by which an experiment becomes a theorem without anyone deciding that it should.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This EXTENDS the existing vocabulary — it does not replace it (ES-005.4, never a copy)
a_rows_sample.statement: The zero-algebra lane already used [EXP]/[OPEN]/[NEG]/[DEF] (plus [PROP]/[THEORY]/[DESIGN]/[DEFECT]); five of eight required categories already existed, so [THM] (theorem, proof cited/contained), [COR] (corollary, cited antecedent + stated derivation), and [CONJ] (conjecture, must state its refutation condition) are added as genuinely new tags rather than duplicating the vocabulary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [PROP] is ambiguous and is retired as a live tag
a_rows_sample.statement: [PROP] collided between 'proposal/recommendation' (KR-BRIDGE-02's usage) and the mathematical sense 'proposition' (a proved statement of lesser weight than a theorem); resolved per the repository's existing legacy-alias pattern (EXPERIMENT-ID-REGISTRY) into [PRP] (Proposition, proved, live) and [REC] (Recommendation, no truth claim, live), with [PROP] retired as a legacy alias only; every existing [PROP] use in the zero-algebra results is confirmed to be the recommendation sense, none a proved proposition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [EXP] NEVER becomes [THM] by accumulating experiments. A theorem needs a PROOF.
a_rows_sample.statement: The promotion ladder is stated as one-directional and gated: [CONJ] -experiment-> [EXP] -proof-> [PRP]/[THM] -derivation-> [COR], with refutation moving anything to [NEG]; [EXP]->[THM] requires a proof not more evidence, stated as a prohibition rather than a caution, and [REC] never becomes anything because it carries no truth claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A design property is not an empirical result
a_rows_sample.statement: Added 2026-09-05 on the research owner's instruction: before tagging any measured quantity [EXP], ask whether the number could have come out differently given the design — if no, it is [DEF], a restatement of the construction; worked corpus instances include context_preserved=1.000 (the operator was designed never to delete), restriction's 0.000 cross-dimension-cause rate (a restricted operator cannot cross its own defining boundary), the 0.87525 'Zero before evidence' rate (identical to the generator's cross-dimension rate, relabelled), and zoom_admissible==zoom_nontrivial at 844/844 (the threshold could not fail).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every experiment reports a DEGENERATE METRICS section naming each such quantity and the mechanism that forces it.
a_rows_sample.statement: New reporting requirement: a results document without a Degenerate Metrics section 'has not looked'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability ≠ Preservation ≠ Realization ... [EXP] — separated experimentally by KR-ZERO, KR-REP-REDUCTION and KR-BRIDGE-01/02. Not [THM]
a_rows_sample.statement: Immediate application §4: the standing 2026-09-04 register is fully re-tagged under the new vocabulary, including the DPI as the sole [THM], its [COR] with the corrected 'structurally inapplicable != empirically falsified' note, FR-001 and FR-003 tagged [EXP], and the flattening-redundancy-increases-informative-strata claim explicitly re-tagged [NEG] per the KR-BRIDGE-03 calibration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: context_preserved = 1.000 must never be written as 'the experiment demonstrated perfect context preservation.'
a_rows_sample.statement: A definitional-vs-evidential distinction: several measured 1.000/0.000 quantities (context preservation, restriction's inability to find cross-dimension causes, the 0.87525 'Zero before evidence' rate that is identical to the generator's cross-dimension rate relabelled) are forced by design and must be reported as such, not as empirical results — now a standing methodological rule referenced to the epistemic-status vocabulary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: governance HAS gained an entry since I last measured: EPISTEMIC-STATUS-VOCABULARY.md — ADOPTED 2026-09-04
a_rows_sample.statement: Withdraws a prior claim that 'governance grew by zero entries', citing the newly adopted epistemic status vocabulary document.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recounted 2026-09-06 across all 16 documents. ⚠️ These are TAG OCCURRENCES, counted mechanically — not distinct statements.
a_rows_sample.statement: A tag-occurrence ledger for the whole set: [EXP] 129, [NEG] 118, [REC] 40, [OPEN] 34, [DEF] 24, [CONJ] 13, [DEFECT] 11, [THM] 8 (referencing one distinct theorem, the DPI, cited eight times), [COR] 6, [PRP] 3, [CORPUS]/[DESIGN] 1/1; the near-1:1 [NEG]-to-[EXP] ratio is read as the point, not the totals — a set where [EXP] outran [NEG] by an order of magnitude would indicate a programme that had stopped testing its own hypotheses.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are three distinct questions. None implies another.
b_rows_sample.statement: The load-bearing result of the Theory 00-14 programme: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))) [Zero/eliminability], Hhat(Q|T(D))=0 [Adequacy/preservation] and O(T(D))=Q(D) [Realization] are shown to differ in every system tested, by independent mechanisms; tagged [EXP] deliberately rather than [THM] because necessity of the separation in general is unproven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
b_rows_sample.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (adequate) is a separate fact from O(R5)=Q(D) (realized): a fixed decoder can fail on information-theoretically adequate data because it was fixed in advance and not refit; flagged as a design defect that the KR-REP-REDUCTION chain never operationalized this separation (no dropped record/source ever made constraint C fail), so 'the separation is real; that experiment could not exhibit it.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Realization ⟹ Adequacy
b_rows_sample.statement: Standing conjecture that if a fixed decoder recovers Q from R on every observed case, R determines Q on the realized cases; refutable by a decoder that is right by luck (correct on every observed case while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous); explicitly 'not tested.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do the separations survive a non-synthetic carrier?
b_rows_sample.statement: Flagged as the central transfer problem: whether eliminability/preservation/realization separations generalize beyond the tested synthetic carrier is explicitly open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The estimand for any bridge claim is the within-stratum effect.
b_rows_sample.statement: The programme's central methodological error was estimating the wrong quantity competently — the marginal P(A|Z)-P(A|not Z) was already known to be confounded before KR-BRIDGE-02 ran; re-estimating it produced a false 'H2 SUPPORTED'; the correct estimand is the Mantel-Haenszel within-stratum effect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
b_rows_sample.statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sign agreement alone is not replication.
b_rows_sample.statement: Under a sign-only replication rule, 14 cells 'replicated' with |RD|~0.001 and 12 of 14 had no stratum CI excluding zero; all 14 collapsed at higher power. Replication requires sign agreement AND clearing a substantive floor on both splits AND at least one stratum's 95% CI excluding zero; per-stratum RDs must be reported, not only the pooled MH estimate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If the floor is declared after first inspection, record that fact in the artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: Effect-size floors must be declared and used as a reporting tier rather than a filter (publish every surviving cell at both tiers) since at n~10^5 statistical significance is not evidence of anything; a post-inspection floor must be disclosed as such.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bootstrap CI on Ĥ ... [DEFECT] invalid here
b_rows_sample.statement: Estimator hygiene register: N_viol is exact and bias-free (authoritative for combinatorial adequacy questions), the Miller-Madow correction is used for Hhat, Haldane+0.5/Woolf CI is used for sparse odds-ratio tables, and bootstrap CI on Hhat is invalid because resampling duplicates cases and depresses conditional entropy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Standard formalized here: never state a regime-specific empirical finding as a general causal law; a single-mechanism explanation of the KR-BRIDGE-01 confound was itself withdrawn once the Zero-count was found constant at r=1 but varying at r=2, showing the exact RD=0 had two different causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Everything in this set is built from six objects and one operator.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theory 01 fixes the six-object signature of the KnowledgeOS transformation carrier: D (data, a finite multiset of records), T (transformation D->R), R=T(D) (representation), Q (inquiry D->Y), Pi (observable R->O), O (decoder R->Y), and C (constraint predicate on R), plus the inquiry frame Pi_frame=(Q,C,O) with O fixed in advance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a record r = (value, source, tag, timestamp)
b_rows_sample.statement: A record in the tested carriers is r=(value,source,tag,timestamp), optionally a derived rank; explicitly flagged as an experimental carrier, not declared to be the mathematical carrier of KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is indexed by (T,Π) and by the subset S; adequacy by (T,Q) and the population; realization by (T,Q,O) and the case.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero, Adequacy and Realization are defined with different index sets and are not three readings of one quantity: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) <=> Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Adequate(T,Q) <=> Hhat(Q|T(D))=0; Realized(T,Q,O) <=> O(T(D))=Q(D).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Every experiment used a deliberately small numerical carrier (|D|<=6) so fibers would collide and adequacy would be measurable; this is a calibration choice, not an ontological one, and the move to documents/claims/entities/relations/provenance/contradictions/temporal states/evidence is the open research problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A transformation family is either sequential (Rk+1 = Tk(Rk)) or parallel (Rk = Tk(D)) — never silently mixed
b_rows_sample.statement: Sequential vs parallel transformation families is a permanent type-discipline rule, load-bearing because the data-processing inequality (document 04) applies to sequential families and not to parallel ones.

a_rows_sample.anchor: When is there enough trustworthy knowledge to make a decision? This is different from asking whether a claim is true. A decision may depend on multiple independently necessary conditions
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the central epistemic-sufficiency question, distinct from claim truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sufficient(K,d) means that the available knowledge satisfies the epistemic conditions required by d. Sufficient(K,d_1) does not imply Sufficient(K,d_2)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines decision-specific epistemic sufficiency, non-transferable across decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(SystemHealthy)=0.95. That might be sufficient for LowRiskPlanning. It may be completely insufficient for SafetyCriticalDeployment. EpistemicSufficiency is decision-specific
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example establishing sufficiency is decision-specific, no universal threshold.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pre(d) = {p_1,...,p_n}. Pre(d) = {IdentityConfirmed, CurrentStateKnown, SecurityValidated, GovernanceApproved}. The decision is admissible only if its required preconditions are satisfied
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines decision preconditions with a four-item worked example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If p_1 is necessary: d=>p_1. But satisfying p_1 does not necessarily imply d. Necessary != Sufficient
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally distinguishes necessary from sufficient conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SecurityValidated may be necessary. But it is not sufficient. We may also require TestingPassed, ArchitectureApproved, RollbackAvailable
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked production-deployment example of multiple necessary-but-not-individually-sufficient conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A,B,C,D are mandatory. Then Sufficient(d) = A and B and C and D. This is the simplest assurance composition
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes conjunctive assurance composition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=True, B=True, C=False, D=True, then Sufficient=False. It does not matter that 75% of the conditions passed. For mandatory conditions, one missing condition can block the decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked weakest-link counterexample: 75% pass rate is still insufficient given one mandatory failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(A)=0.99, Assurance(B)=0.99, Assurance(C)=0.10. An average gives 0.693. That does not mean 69.3% safe. The low-assurance critical condition may be decisive
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample warning against averaging assurance scores, which masks a decisive low-assurance condition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Criticality(p_i). But we should not simply multiply all probabilities together unless the probabilistic assumptions justify doing so. Mathematical composition requires semantic assumptions
a_rows_sample.statement: States criticality-weighted composition requires justified semantic assumptions, not blind multiplication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance = (Claim, Evidence, Method, Context, Time, Uncertainty, Validation, Scope). The scalar can be derived when appropriate
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines assurance as a structured eight-field object rather than a bare scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceRequirement(d). Decision: Production Deployment. Required: Identity confirmed, Architecture approved, Security validated, Tests passed, Rollback demonstrated, Governance authorized. This is much closer to executable governance
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents a worked executable evidence-requirement specification for production deployment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KS(K,d) in {True,False,Unknown}. Because sometimes we cannot establish whether the requirements are satisfied. Unknown must not silently become False or True
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines knowledge sufficiency as a three-valued predicate preventing Unknown from silently collapsing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: mathbb L_3 = {T,F,U}. T=established true; F=established false; U=unknown/undetermined. This is particularly useful for incomplete knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines three-valued epistemic logic L3.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A simplified three-valued conjunction: T/T=T, T/F=F, T/U=U, F/T=F, F/F=F, F/U=F, U/T=U, U/F=F, U/U=U. This is more appropriate than forcing missing knowledge into false
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full three-valued conjunction truth table.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Similarly disjunction: T/T=T, T/F=T, T/U=T, F/T=T, F/F=F, F/U=U, U/T=T, U/F=U, U/U=U. This allows reasoning with incomplete information
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full three-valued disjunction truth table.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IdentityConfirmed=T, SecurityValidated=T, RollbackDemonstrated=U. Then Sufficient=False if rollback is mandatory, or Unknown if the policy itself does not establish whether rollback is mandatory
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example applying three-valued conjunction to a concrete deployment decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gate(d,K). Possible states: Pass, Fail, Blocked, Unknown
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a decision gate as a four-state predicate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A gate can pass epistemically while the decision remains unauthorized. GatePass != Authorization. This reinforces Step 40
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes gate-pass from authorization, reinforcing Step 40's authority-vs-truth distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(d) = Compose(A_1,A_2,A_3). But the composition rule must be explicit
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes assurance composition as requiring an explicit composition rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inference asks what can we conclude from what we know. Step 34 asks What should we learn next? ... a fundamentally different problem
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference from information-acquisition selection as fundamentally different problems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10^6 uncertain assertions ... impossible and unnecessary to validate all of them immediately ... Choose the information acquisition action that produces the greatest useful improvement relative to its cost
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS should not investigate everything, requiring a cost-relative optimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: QueryCMDB, InspectRuntime, AskDomainExpert, RunTest, PerformExperiment, RetrieveDocument, CompareIndependentSource ... produces an observation Y_I
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the information-gathering action set with seven worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cost(I) ... Time, Money, Compute, HumanAttention, OperationalRisk ... information is not free
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Cost(I) across five components.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVPI=L_0-L_{PI} ... an upper bound on the value of information
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Perfect Information as an upper bound.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=L_0-E_Y[\min_d E[L(d,\theta)\mid K,Y]] ... NVOI(I)=EVSI(I)-Cost(I) ... the core mathematical idea
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Sample Information and net value of information as the step's core idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I^*=\arg\max_{I\in\mathcal I}NVOI(I) ... our first formal definition of NextBestEpistemicAction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first formal Next-Best-Epistemic-Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: InformationValue\neq UncertaintyReduction ... A has no influence on any important decision ... UncertaintyReduction(A) may have almost zero practical value
b_rows_sample.statement: States the subtle principle that information value is not the same as uncertainty reduction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionSensitivity(A,D) ... Information about A is valuable if learning A can change d^*
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines DecisionSensitivity as the criterion for information value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus has 31 GB RAM ... migration architecture does not depend on RAM beyond a very large safety margin ... almost no decision value
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of low-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (RAM precision beyond safety margin).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Production database backup is restorable ... DecisionSensitivity(B,D) is very high ... validating B may have extremely high VOI
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting example of high-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (backup restorability).

b_rows_sample.anchor: d^*=f(K) ... If perturbing A does not change f(K), then A has low local decision sensitivity
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a decision-relevance partition via perturbation of the decision function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Closure(A) ... A\rightarrow B\rightarrow D ... DependencyClosure+DecisionCriticality=EpistemicPrioritization
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines Step 32's dependency closure with decision dependency, giving a prioritization formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Criticality(D) ... Low, Medium, High, Critical ... should be domain-owned. KnowledgeOS can consume it but should not invent the business meaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a domain-owned Criticality classification, not invented by KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL(d)=E[L(d,\theta)\mid K] ... d^*=\arg\min_d EL(d) ... d_1 expected loss 10, d_2 expected loss 12 ... investigation may reveal a high-risk state in which d_2 becomes preferable
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines expected loss and current-optimal decision, worked with a two-decision expected-loss-reversal example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk<5\%\Rightarrow AutomaticApproval ... Risk\in[3\%,8\%] ... DecisionBoundaryUncertainty. Uncertainty far from a decision boundary may be harmless. Uncertainty near a boundary can be critical
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DecisionBoundaryUncertainty, worked with a threshold-straddling risk-interval example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk\in[1\%,2\%] ... no urgent investigation ... Risk\in[4\%,7\%] crosses the decision boundary ... additional evidence is valuable
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting examples of harmless-far and critical-boundary-straddling risk intervals.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(A)\propto DecisionImpact(A)\times Uncertainty(A) ... conceptual, not yet a universal formula
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual, not-yet-universal epistemic-triage priority formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=10, Cost(I)=2, NVOI(I)=8 ... EVSI=12, Cost=20, NVOI=-8 ... should not be prioritized merely because it provides more information
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked arithmetic example showing higher-EVSI investigations can have lower net value once cost is subtracted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HumanAttention is an epistemic resource ... 2 hours of a senior architect's time may be more expensive than a machine-readable check
b_rows_sample.statement: States human attention is itself a costed epistemic resource, worked with a comparison example.

a_aliases: Epistemic Sufficiency, Decision Preconditions, Assurance Composition and the Mathematics of Enough Knowledge
b_aliases: Information Acquisition, Value of Information, Active Learning and the Next-Best Epistemic Action

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is one additional missing bridge ... Adequacy -> Executability ... we need one more formal relation: ExecutableAdequacy. EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) meaning: the representation and operations together can answer the required questions while preserving every required distinction and producing an auditable transition. This is the real bridge from representation theory to kernel theory. Without it, ABK-1 can be perfectly adequate as a representation while still being insufficient as a kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Executable Adequacy EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) as a proposed missing formal relation between representation-adequacy theory and kernel theory: the representation K and operations O together must be able to answer the required questions Q while preserving every required distinction AND producing an auditable transition; without EA, a representation (e.g. ABK-1) could be perfectly Adequate(R,Q,Gamma) while still being insufficient as a kernel.

type_signature.domain: (representation K, operations O, question Q, context Gamma)

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would now run exactly four final controlled closure packages: C1 -- Evaluation + Determination ... C2 -- Contr + Boundary ... C3 -- Operations + delta + Composition ... C4 -- Equivalence + Executable Adequacy + Reduction, then perform: Reduction -> Kernel Selection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a four-package closure plan replacing the larger roadmap: C1 closes EVal->Det while preserving Truth!=Evaluation!=Determination; C2 closes Contr's isolation meaning without falsely identifying Contr with FDE; C3 determines which operations are genuinely state-transforming (O_core) and defines delta:K x O_core x Gamma -> K', explicitly allowing Composition to remain parameterized/underdetermined if evidence does not select one rule; C4 defines equiv_sem^{Q,Gamma,O} and Executable Adequacy, then finally performs Reduction -> Kernel Selection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Final verdict: Can we close now? No -- not Theory v1.3. But we can close the discovery phase permanently now ... Discovery: CLOSED. Required-distinction foundation: CLOSED. Representation candidate: CLOSED/VALIDATED. Contr/EVal: substantially reconstructed, but overclaimed in the document. Determination: missing. Operations/delta: missing. Composition: unresolved. Semantic equivalence: unresolved. Executable adequacy: missing bridge. Kernel reduction/selection: not yet possible. Theory v1.3: NOT READY.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final consolidated status verdict: Discovery is CLOSED, the required-distinction foundation is CLOSED, the representation candidate (ABK-1) is CLOSED/VALIDATED as a representation only; Contr and EVal are substantially reconstructed but overclaimed in the reviewed document; Determination, Operations/delta, Composition, Semantic equivalence, and Executable Adequacy remain missing/unresolved; Kernel reduction/selection is not yet possible; Theory v1.3 is explicitly NOT READY.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B1 Composition: BLOCKED -- Depends on O3 and O4 ... B2 Executable Adequacy: ExecutableAdequacy(K,O,Q,Gamma) definition, bridge between representation theory and kernel theory, auditability requirement -- BLOCKED, Depends on O1, O2, O3, O4 ... B3 Kernel Reduction: BLOCKED -- Depends on all open items ... B4 Kernel Selection: BLOCKED -- Depends on B3.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records four items as BLOCKED pending resolution of the OPEN items: Composition (depends on O_core and delta), Executable Adequacy (depends on Determination, Semantic Equivalence, O_core, and delta), Kernel Reduction (depends on all open items), and Kernel Selection (depends on Kernel Reduction) -- establishing an explicit dependency ordering across the whole remaining closure chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package 4: Equivalence + Executable Adequacy + Reduction ... Define Executable Adequacy -> SPEC-EXEC-ADEQ-2026-v1.0 ... Produce Theory v1.3 -> THEORY-v1.3-2026-09-02.md
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a concrete expected artifact for Executable Adequacy, SPEC-EXEC-ADEQ-2026-v1.0, as part of Package 4 (alongside SPEC-EQUIV, SPEC-KERNEL, SPEC-KERNEL-SELECT, and the eventual THEORY-v1.3-2026-09-02.md), the first time this batch names a specific document for the Executable Adequacy concept introduced in the immediately preceding review file.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D. The Missing Bridge: Executable Adequacy (EA) ... EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) iff Adequacy(K,Q,Gamma) and forall op in O, Preserved(delta(K,op,Gamma),Gamma) supseteq R_req(Q,Gamma). An adequate representation K is Executably Adequate only if the operational set O and transition function delta preserve all required distinctions R_req across state transformations without introducing silent collapse.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the first fully quantified formal definition of Executable Adequacy: EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) holds iff K is representation-Adequate for (Q,Gamma) AND for every operation op in O, applying delta(K,op,Gamma) preserves at least R_req(Q,Gamma) -- i.e. no operation may silently collapse a required distinction across a state transformation.

type_signature.domain: (representation K, operation set O, question Q, context Gamma)

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would reduce everything to five final research/closure problems, not nine documents. CLOSURE-1 EVALUATION ... CLOSURE-2 DETERMINATION ... CLOSURE-3 TRANSFORMATION: Close jointly O_core + delta because operation identity cannot be completely specified independently of transition semantics ... CLOSURE-4 EQUIVALENCE + COMPOSITION ... CLOSURE-5 EXECUTABLE ADEQUACY -> KERNEL.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reduces the roadmap's nine independent SPEC documents to five explicitly coupled closure problems: CLOSURE-1 Evaluation, CLOSURE-2 Determination, CLOSURE-3 Transformation (O_core and delta closed jointly, since operation identity cannot be independently specified from transition semantics), CLOSURE-4 Equivalence+Composition, CLOSURE-5 Executable Adequacy->Kernel; explicitly recommends NOT producing seven independent giant SPEC documents (SPEC-EVAL through SPEC-KERNEL) since several are mathematically coupled and treating them independently would reproduce the original problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A candidate kernel K* is acceptable only if it satisfies: Preserve(R_req) and Eval defined and Det defined and O_core supported and delta defined and Composition characterized and Equivalence defined and Provenance preserved. Then, and only then: ExecutableAdequacy -> KernelReduction -> KernelSelection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives an eight-conjunct acceptance criterion for a candidate kernel K*: it must preserve R_req, have Eval and Det defined, support O_core, have delta defined, have Composition characterized (not necessarily uniquely resolved), have Equivalence defined, and preserve Provenance -- only after all eight hold can ExecutableAdequacy->KernelReduction->KernelSelection proceed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EA(K,O_core,Q,Gamma) iff Psi_Soundness and Psi_Isolation and Psi_Termination and Psi_Determinism ... 1. Soundness & Monotonicity ... 2. Structural Isolation Soundness: forall q in Scope(Contr(p),Gamma), Q(q,delta(K_t,ISOLATE(p),Gamma)) = <S(q),ContradictionTrapped> ... 3. Bounded Termination: exists C, T(Q,K,Gamma) <= C*(|Nodes(K)|+|Edges(K)|) ... 4. Deterministic Audit Traceability: Replay(K_0,mu_{0..t})=K_t implies H(Replay(...))=H(K_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Executable Adequacy into a conjunction of four named dimensional predicates: Psi_Soundness (node monotonicity across O_core), Psi_Isolation (firewalled queries always return ContradictionTrapped without exception leakage), Psi_Termination (query/update time polynomially bounded by graph size, T<=C*(|Nodes|+|Edges|)), and Psi_Determinism (replaying the full audit log from the initial state reproduces the identical state hash) -- each independently falsifiable.

type_signature.codomain: boolean EA = AND of four sub-predicates

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 equiv_Gamma K2 iff forall q in P, EVal(q,K1,Q,Gamma) = EVal(q,K2,Q,Gamma) ... Reflexivity: K equiv_Gamma K ... Symmetry ... Transitivity ... Contextual Relaxation: If Gamma' subset Gamma, then K1 equiv_Gamma K2 implies K1 equiv_Gamma' K2.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Parameterized Semantic Equivalence: K1 equiv_Gamma K2 iff they produce identical EVal results for every proposition under context Gamma; verifies the standard equivalence-relation axioms (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity) and adds a Contextual Relaxation axiom -- equivalence under a broader context Gamma implies equivalence under any tighter sub-context Gamma' subset Gamma.

type_signature.domain: two knowledge states K1,K2 and context Gamma

b_rows_sample.anchor: Final Kernel Reduction Matrix: With the execution of Closure Packages C1 through C4, the KnowledgeOS Kernel reduction is complete ... C1 Truth & Evidence Space ... C2 Contradiction & Scope ... C3 Operations Algebra ... C4 Equivalence & Adequacy ... PACKAGE C4 FALSIFICATION TEST: PASSED (EA and Equivalence verified)
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues the file's culminating claim: 'With the execution of Closure Packages C1 through C4, the KnowledgeOS Kernel reduction is complete', supported by a final matrix summarizing each package's formal result and a Python test (test_c4_adequacy_and_equivalence) reported PASSED for both Executable Adequacy and Semantic Equivalence on a small synthetic three-operation example; status self-declared [RATIFIED -- FINAL CLOSURE PACKAGE] for C4 specifically, versus [RATIFICATION CANDIDATE] for C2 and C3 in the same file.
