Note: Finding that the proposed invariant universe I is not a single mathematical object: transition invariants (schema-shaped, requiring an admissible operation o) and layer/type invariants (statically shaped, holding independent of any transition, e.g. Reality != Observation != Knower) are incompatible kinds, and forcing a layer invariant into the transition schema would make it vacuously true since the antecedent never engages it -- merging the two under one symbol I is a category error.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DI principle vs framework import: adopt the DI/composition-root principle without adopting Spring — the corpus wants the first, but the kernel file pairs the principle with the Spring runtime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
b_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
b_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
b_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
b_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kernel-cost-vs-invariant-justification-tension' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-kernel-concept' (batch B0032). Note: The observation that Kernel-inclusion arguments split into two types -- cost/economics arguments (reward more Kernel content) and invariant/protection arguments (reward less/minimal Kernel content) -- which can yield opposite verdicts from the same evidence; flagged as a standing caution across the Session-2 review register.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document currently conflates: KnowledgeOS Domain ... Application/Governance ... Interpretation mechanisms ... Kernel infrastructure ... The uploaded document puts almost all of these into 'Kernel.'
a_rows_sample.statement: The prior constitutional-knowledge-engine proposal (S0358/S0359) is diagnosed as conflating four distinct layers — the KnowledgeOS domain proper, Application/Governance orchestration, Interpretation mechanisms, and Kernel infrastructure — into a single overloaded 'Kernel' responsibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A judge does not normally: tokenize language, parse syntax, retrieve databases, persist state, execute infrastructure, manage workflow. Yet this proposal gives the Kernel all of those responsibilities.
a_rows_sample.statement: The 'proposal→facts→law→verdict→execution' judge metaphor is warned to be dangerous if taken literally, because a real judge does not tokenize, parse, persist, execute infrastructure, or manage workflow — those responsibilities must be separated out of the Kernel even though the adjudication metaphor itself remains useful.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An intent is what the human appears to mean. A command is an authorized request to change domain state. Those are fundamentally different concepts. ... only after governance evaluation should we get: AuthorizedCommand: StartAdoptionReview
a_rows_sample.statement: A DDD distinction is proposed between an Intent Candidate (what the human appears to mean, produced by Interpretation) and an Authorized Command (an authorized request to change domain state, produced only after Governance Evaluation) — refining the earlier pipeline from 'raw proposal→Intent AST→constitutional validation→execution' into an eight-stage pipeline ending in a Domain Event.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Priority rules' also need DDD scrutiny ... Why should 'identity' outrank 'history'? ... Who owns those priorities? ... DDD tells us to discover the meaning and ownership of the rule first. Only afterward should we decide how rules are represented.
a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed integer rule-priority ordering is challenged not on implementation grounds but on ownership grounds: before representing priorities as sortable integers, the domain question of who owns and justifies that ordering (constitutional law vs application policy vs evaluation strategy) must be answered first.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is Kernel implementation history part of the KnowledgeOS domain? Probably not. ... KnowledgeOS history ≠ Kernel software history. ... Software versioning belongs to the engineering system. Knowledge state belongs to KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: The prior proposal's 'self-audit'/self-versioning idea (the Kernel versions its own code as knowledge state) is rejected: Kernel software-implementation history and KnowledgeOS domain knowledge-state history are distinct concepts that may be linked via provenance but must never be conflated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would reject that sequencing for now. Not because the technology is bad. Because it is implementation-first. ... Building a DSL before answering those questions risks making the DSL become the architecture. That would invert DDD.
a_rows_sample.statement: The prior proposal's five-phase implementation sequencing (Constitutional DSL → Intent Parser → Constitutional Resolver → Trust Layer → Execution Layer) is explicitly rejected as implementation-first; domain concepts (aggregate, invariant, governance rule, interpretation mechanism, command, evidence, authority, boundary) must be answered before any DSL is built, else the DSL becomes the architecture by default.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is architectural conflation at scale. The proposal treats the Kernel as a 'god object' that owns nearly every important capability in the system. ... The core error is treating a useful architectural metaphor (the constitutional adjudicator) as a domain concept, then using it as a container for every responsibility that seemed important.
a_rows_sample.statement: A formal DDD critical review names the core methodological error in the prior Constitutional Kernel proposal: an architectural metaphor (constitutional adjudicator) was treated as a domain concept and then used as a container for every responsibility that seemed important, producing a 'god object.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conflation 1: Interpretation ≠ Adjudication ... Conflation 2: Evidence Evaluation ≠ Evidence Preservation ... Conflation 3: Constitutional Rules ≠ Rule Engine ... Conflation 4: Adjudication ≠ Execution ... Conflation 5: Self-Audit ≠ Domain Responsibility ... Conflation 6: History ≠ Provenance ≠ Audit Log
a_rows_sample.statement: Six named conflations are identified and separated: natural-language parsing is a mechanism not a domain concept; numeric evidence weighting is mechanism-confidence not epistemic confidence; the constitution is domain policy while the rule engine is infrastructure; determining admissibility and executing the transition are different responsibilities; self-audit of the Kernel's own software is an infrastructure concern, not a domain one; and domain history, provenance, audit log, and event sourcing are four separately-owned concepts collapsed into one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate Bounded Contexts: Expression Context, Interpretation Context, Governance Context, Knowledge Context, Workflow Context, Evidence Context, Audit Context
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven candidate bounded contexts are proposed with an ownership-by-concept table (KnowledgeAggregate/Identity/Provenance/Contradiction owned only by Knowledge Context; Meaning Candidate/Intent owned by Interpretation Context; Constitutional Rules owned by Governance Context; Command owned by Application Context), explicitly labelled CANDIDATE, not established architecture, pending validation against the existing KnowledgeOS/EKS landscape.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Falsification Table ... 1. Kernel should parse proposals → MOVE OUT ... 4. Kernel should weight evidence numerically → MOVE OUT ... 5. Kernel should resolve contradictions → SPLIT (detect in Kernel, resolve in Governance) ... 7. Kernel should own immutable history → KEEP (domain history only)
a_rows_sample.statement: A ten-row falsification table judges each claim from the prior Constitutional Kernel proposal as MOVE OUT (7 claims: parsing, candidate generation, semantic interpretation, numeric evidence weighting, execution, self-audit, GLR parsing), SPLIT (2 claims: contradiction resolution, constitutional DSL), or KEEP (1 claim, domain history only), yielding the restricted Kernel definition: identity, state-transition admissibility, history, provenance, contradiction detection, evidence-reference preservation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Kernel = pure function' → HYPOTHESIS, not decision. ... A pure admissibility function and a domain aggregate are not necessarily the same thing.
a_rows_sample.statement: A subsequent challenge to the DDD critical review itself downgrades its conclusion that 'the Kernel is a pure function from (command, state, rules, evidence) to admissibility verdict' from an accepted decision to an open hypothesis, arguing the Kernel likely needs both a domain model (identity/state/provenance/contradiction/history/events) and a deterministic adjudication operation, not merely the latter.

a_rows_sample.anchor: adjudicate(state₁, command) → admissible ... something happens ... execute(state₂, command) ... The state could have changed between adjudication and application.
a_rows_sample.statement: Separating adjudication from execution too aggressively risks a transactional gap: the aggregate's state could change between the moment admissibility is determined and the moment the transition is actually applied, so who owns the actual state mutation (Kernel vs Application/Workflow) needs a stronger transactional answer than a simple 'Kernel says ADMISSIBLE, then Application executes' handoff.

a_rows_sample.anchor: if Governance simply sends an arbitrary rule set to the Kernel ... the Kernel is effectively saying: 'I will accept whatever someone calls the Constitution.' That isn't necessarily safe. ... 'The Kernel evaluates a transition against the authoritative constitutional policy applicable to that transition.'
a_rows_sample.statement: The critique's formulation 'the Kernel applies the rules as provided by the Governance Context' is challenged as unsafe because it implies the Kernel would accept whatever rule set is handed to it; the formulation is corrected to require the Kernel evaluate against the authoritative constitutional policy applicable to the transition, with source/certification/version/admissibility of that policy remaining governed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DeepSeek invented some bounded contexts ... These are candidate contexts, not established architecture. ... DDD says: discover bounded contexts from domain boundaries and language; don't manufacture them from architectural neatness.
a_rows_sample.statement: The seven proposed bounded contexts (Expression/Interpretation/Governance/Knowledge/Workflow/Evidence/Audit) are flagged as the review's biggest methodological risk — invented from conceptual neatness rather than discovered from actual domain boundaries and existing ubiquitous language — and must be labelled CANDIDATE BOUNDED CONTEXTS pending validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The core error is **treating a useful architectural metaphor (the constitutional adjudicator) as a domain concept**, then using it as a container for every responsibility.
a_rows_sample.statement: A DeepSeek-generated P6 critique diagnoses the prior 'Constitutional Kernel' proposal as a god object combining natural-language intent parsing, constitutional rule evaluation, state transition execution, history management, contradiction resolution, evidence weighting, and self-audit, naming the root cause as metaphor-treated-as-domain-concept, and concluding 'the Kernel is only the Knowledge Context responsibility.' The project's own response (Part B) accepts the diagnosis but explicitly refuses to accept DeepSeek's final Kernel definition, calling instead for DDD reconciliation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: History ≠ Provenance ≠ Audit Log
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate non-collapse distinctions: (1) Interpretation != Adjudication, (2) Evidence Evaluation != Evidence Preservation and Mechanism Confidence != Epistemic Confidence != Evidence, (3) Constitutional Rules != Rule Engine (Domain Policy != Implementation Mechanism), (4) Adjudication != Execution, (5) Self-Audit != Domain Responsibility, (6) History != Provenance != Audit Log. Cross-checked against v1.1: (1),(3),(5) CONSISTENT; (2) PARTIALLY CONSISTENT (bears on unruled W:C-11, a three-way confidence split not among the eleven invariants); (4) and (6) NOT ADDRESSED as named rows, recorded as the corpus's own candidate contribution (bearing on W:C-2/DEF-1 and unruled W:C-15 respectively), not proposed as amendments.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the artifact counts **rows** and reports them as **conflations**
a_rows_sample.statement: The six conflation-table rows state more than six distinctions (row 2 contains a three-way split Mechanism-Confidence!=Epistemic-Confidence!=Evidence in addition to Evidence-Evaluation!=Evidence-Preservation; row 6 contains a three-way split History!=Provenance!=Audit-Log plus a separable ownership claim), while rows 1/3/5 all instantiate one untested principle (mechanism/quality-attribute is not a domain responsibility) and may be one restated distinction rather than three independent ones -- so the stated-distinction count exceeds six while the independent-distinction count is plausibly around three families, the same counting-defect family as S2-F017 in the opposite direction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the project accepted the diagnosis and refused the prescription
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F007's quotations ('this is a very useful result', 'we are much closer to the Kernel definition than we were before', 'the next step is DDD reconciliation') support only the refusal of the final definition, not acceptance of the six-conflation diagnosis; useful and accepted are distinct claims, so S1-F007's weight-ranking ('the six conflations carry more corpus weight than any Kernel definition offered alongside them') inherits an over-read. Defensible restatement: the project refused the prescription and did not record a verdict on the diagnosis. Also reclassifies row 4 (Adjudication!=Execution) from 'NOT ADDRESSED' to 'addressed by inclusion' since v1.1 section 16 places both refuse-a-transition and record-state/assign-identity/retain-history inside one kernel enumeration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A database says store(x). KnowledgeOS must additionally support something like discriminate(x). ... Kernel ~ Manas + Buddhi-like epistemic processing ... not Kernel=Mind ... not Kernel=all intelligence ... a constitutional epistemic substrate around language, reasoning, planning, simulation and learning -- not the whole brain.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Gita lens changes the conceptual architecture: a database supports store(x); KnowledgeOS must additionally support discriminate(x). The kernel is philosophically analogous to Mind, more precisely Kernel ~ Manas + Buddhi-like epistemic processing -- explicitly NOT Kernel=Mind and definitely NOT Kernel=all intelligence; the existing architecture already positions KnowledgeOS as a constitutional epistemic substrate around language, reasoning, planning, simulation and learning, not the whole 'brain.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel != Knowledge Store. Instead: Kernel = State + Discrimination + Transformation ... K_t -Buddhi-> K_{t+1} ... Given what is currently known, observed, asserted, related and constrained, what should be accepted, rejected, transformed, investigated, or acted upon?
a_rows_sample.statement: Kernel != Knowledge Store; instead Kernel = State + Discrimination + Transformation, formalized K_t --Buddhi--> K_{t+1}, with the kernel continuously asking what should be accepted/rejected/transformed/investigated/acted upon given current knowledge, observations, assertions, relations and constraints.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "The current language is not yet completely stabilized. **This is itself an architectural finding.**"
b_rows_sample.statement: The project's own 2026-08-21 architecture document tabulates 20 terms with recorded ambiguity (e.g. Knowledge: 'broad, current representation boundaries unclear'; Authority: 'current mechanism records it rather than creating it'; Human Act: 'current mechanism cannot create it'; Artifact: 'broad, not equivalent to knowledge'), and separately finds 'Rule' used for seven materially different concepts (engineering standards, rulings, architecture principles, recommendation heuristics, quality-gate rules, document-validation rules, permission rules), concluding this is a DDD vocabulary problem, not a naming problem, and prescribing 'preserve these distinctions rather than prematurely normalizing them.' This method rule anticipated, four days early, the vocabulary collisions this reconstruction programme later found independently (projection in three senses, agent in two, UNKNOWN at two altitudes).

b_rows_sample.anchor: the mechanism **records** authority rather than **creating** it ... cannot **create** a Human Act ... **Three independent arrivals** at: *the system can record, not manufacture.*
b_rows_sample.statement: Two entries bear directly on authority: the mechanism records authority rather than creating it, and cannot create a Human Act — the same limit as KCON-018 ('no authority manufacture') and KCON-013 (recorded difference ≠ actual independence), reached independently — three independent arrivals at 'the system can record, not manufacture.' Also: 'Artifact not equivalent to knowledge' is an early statement of representation≠knowledge, consistent with formal law's Representation≠Identity/Expression≠Meaning (§15).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The current authority record is strong in provenance but weak in temporal semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measured over 20 observed authority grants: grants with human-act reference 20/20, registeredBy=governance 20/20, grants with immutable commit addressing 13/20, using descriptive artifact references 7/20 — but grants with validity information 0/20, delegation information 0/20, ownership information 0/20. Consequence, in the source's own words: the system 'can establish that authority was registered against a human act, but cannot reliably answer: was this authority valid at a particular historical point in time' — explicitly 'a current-state limitation, not a future-architecture opinion.' By the project's own evidence hierarchy (20260801-1231 §3) this is implementation/persistence-derived evidence (priority 1-3), the strongest evidence class encountered in the corpus so far.

b_rows_sample.anchor: can the system reconstruct the validity of an authority at a past instant?" — currently, no, at 0/20.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the corpus's temporal question, previously philosophical (knowledge-at-a-time, projection, evolving Knowledge Space, all Phase 2 hypothesis), into a narrower measured one: 'can the system reconstruct the validity of an authority at a past instant?' — currently no, at 0/20. Sharpens KCON-017 (record existence ≠ authority establishment, same day 20260821-2032): registration is recorded, but validity over time is not — independently arrived at. Classifies against formal law: W:C-18 (constitutional-version binding is precisely a temporal validity claim, currently lacking); W:C-3 (authority adequacy at which time is undefined); W:C-15 (retraction/withdrawal, same family — what the record says later); v1.1 comparison: NOT ADDRESSED, since v1.1 does not speak to authority validity intervals.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If the grant record has no field in which validity could be expressed, then `0/20` is not twenty observations. It is a single structural fact — the schema cannot represent validity — encountered twenty times.
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F001's '0/20' validity-information figure reads as a measured empirical rate, inviting 'would a larger sample find some?' — but since the grant record schema has no field capable of expressing validity, 0/20 is one structural fact (schema cannot represent validity) encountered twenty times, not twenty independent observations. Evidence: three independent properties (validity, delegation, ownership) all land at exactly zero across twenty records — the signature of representational absence, not measurement — while properties that ARE representable vary normally (human-act reference 20/20, immutable commit addressing 13/20, descriptive references 7/20); the variation pattern itself distinguishes the two kinds of zero. Connects to the Zero lens: 'absence of the means of expression' is a different thing from 'absence of a value', and S1-F001's original framing conflates them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: These are three different temporal questions with three different subjects. Grouping them invites a single answer to what needs three.
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F001 groups W:C-18 (version binding), W:C-3 (authority adequacy), and W:C-15 (retraction) as one family on the ground that all concern 'what the record says later' — but these are three different questions with three different subjects: was the authority valid at T (the grant's own validity interval); was the claim valid at T (TemporalValidity, already modelled); does the claimant still assert it (the agent's stance, neither of the above). Evidence the three vary independently: a claim may remain within valid-from/valid-until, admitted under a never-lapsed authority, and still be withdrawn by its asserter; conversely an authority may lapse while the claimant's stance is unchanged — the standard test for one-concept-vs-three.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus's own recorded method rule — quoted in `S1-F002` — is "**preserve these distinctions rather than prematurely normalizing them**"... **S1-F001 groups where S1-F002 warns against grouping.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Flags that S1-F001 (S0588) and S1-F002 (S0587) — the same source document, the same day — are in tension on method: S1-F002 records the rule 'preserve distinctions rather than prematurely normalizing them' and names over-grouping a DDD vocabulary problem, yet S1-F001 groups three independently-varying temporal questions into one family, violating the rule its sibling finding just recorded. Recommends recording the 'family' as three adjacent questions sharing a lens, not one family sharing an answer. Explicitly does not overwrite Session 1's grouping — records the challenge as OPEN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: v1.1 *does* carry temporal validity — for the **claim**... So the model provides a validity interval for **what is asserted**, and none for **the authority under which it was asserted**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects S1-F001's classification of the v1.1 comparison as 'NOT ADDRESSED — v1.1 does not speak to authority validity intervals': that is right about authority but misses the asymmetry. v1.1's TemporalValidity (valid-from/valid-until/superseded-by, Article 11, 'freshness never truth, expiry never absence') is an aggregate member giving the CLAIM an explicit validity interval, while Authority is merely a reference ('a recorded reference to a human act; held by the Authority context, referenced by the aggregate') carrying no interval — 'A claim can be asked were you valid at T? The authority that admitted it cannot.' S1-F001's measured 0/20 baseline exhibits the same asymmetry the target model itself has.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The gap is therefore **not a baseline defect that the target model fixes**. It is present in both, which changes its status: from "the current system is behind" to "neither the current system nor the target model time-indexes authority."
b_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies the finding from NOT ADDRESSED to 'ADDRESSED FOR THE CLAIM, NOT FOR THE AUTHORITY': the temporal-validity gap is not a baseline defect the target model fixes but a property present in both — the question is not whether the model CAN express intervals (it demonstrably can, for claims) but why the concept is applied to one side of an admission (the claim) and not the other (the authority). Explicit governance boundary: 'This finding must not be routed into the active adjudication. The corpus is sealed for that purpose; this is a review record' — research relevance only, no element proposed, Session 1's document not modified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **`Knowledge`** — *"Broad; current representation boundaries unclear"*
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F002's table records, as its first row, that 'Knowledge' itself has 'unclear representation boundaries', with two adjacent rows compounding it (Observation: relationship to evidence/knowledge not fully formalized; Artifact: broad, not equivalent to knowledge) — meaning the baseline cannot cleanly bound Knowledge against evidence, observation, or artifact. S1-F002 draws out only the Artifact≠Knowledge row and does not connect it back to the Knowledge row it qualifies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A project whose central term is recorded by its own baseline as having unclear representation boundaries has stated something more consequential than that `Rule` is overloaded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reading the table with the Knowledge row foregrounded changes what the table is: from evidence of vocabulary instability (a method finding) to evidence about the subject matter itself — the baseline could not say where knowledge ends and evidence, observation, or artifact begin. This also supplies the strongest available support for S1-F002's own 'preserve, do not prematurely normalize' method rule, since the term at stake (Knowledge) is more consequential than the term S1-F002 argued from (Rule).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Only Evidence and Provenance survive both lists.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two Phase 1 Kernel member-list proposals 36 minutes apart (20:32 and 21:08, 2026-08-21): Document A — kernel as 'a deterministic runtime for governed knowledge state, authority, evidence, lifecycle and provenance' (members: authority mechanics, generic evidence mechanics, lifecycle, provenance); Document B — kernel as 'observation/evaluation mechanics with rules pushed out to a port' (members: Observation, Evidence, Rule evaluation protocol, Assessment, Result, Provenance). Only Evidence and Provenance appear in both; Authority and Lifecycle are in A only, Observation/Assessment/Result/Rule-evaluation are in B only. B is a self-declared revision of A after consulting an older baseline document, not an independent arrival. Caution recorded: the {Evidence, Provenance} intersection is a historical fact about two proposals, not a minimality result or a finding about the Kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: may be a particularly important kernel abstraction
b_rows_sample.statement: ChangeSet, from Document B, deliberately separates event detection from observation execution and is source-agnostic (does not care whether the change originated from VS Code, Claude Code, Git, or another tool) — an implemented mechanism, evidence priority 1-3 rather than 7. Explicit caution: 'implemented ≠ Kernel-authoritative' — implementation raises evidence class but confers no architectural standing; a mechanism can be real, useful, source-agnostic, and still belong outside the Kernel boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the kernel holds the port; EKS and PKS supply the rules
b_rows_sample.statement: Rule Port, from Document B: Kernel → Observation → Rule Port → {EKS engineering rules | PKS product rules}; concrete rules (LCOM4, test-presence, architecture, DDD) and the engineering-recommendation engine are explicitly kept outside the kernel. Classified as CONSISTENT with v1.1's later Verification Port and its mechanism-altitude separation (§16), reached independently one day earlier; recorded as a convergence to accumulate, not a ruling.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the actual relationship between the existing EKS runtime, the existing AI Engineering Platform, PKS, and the proposed KnowledgeOS kernel?
b_rows_sample.statement: Document B corrects the framing question from 'what parts of EKS can we move into the KnowledgeOS kernel?' to 'what is the actual relationship between the existing EKS runtime, AIP, PKS, and the proposed kernel?', on the ground that multiple architectural mechanisms already look like kernel primitives; also states '.claude definitely should not become the kernel' and 'the correct next phase is therefore NOT EP-01.' The reviewer notes the corpus was already resisting deriving the Kernel by relocating existing code rather than by identifying what must be protected.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No mature research field appears to define a universally accepted: `knowledge kernel` · `epistemic kernel` · `organizational memory kernel`.
b_rows_sample.statement: An independent external-research review (20260821-2351, self-declared P2 external evidence base, not a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal) finds the term 'knowledge kernel' exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work, and concludes KnowledgeOS is 'not entering an established category.' Consequence: every Kernel property must be justified internally, since there is no external field to appeal to for validation, and nothing established to converge on.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Weak Analogy Areas" because "Knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution
b_rows_sample.statement: Material contradiction (candidate): Position A (20260821-2032, P1, 20:32) claims the kernel is 'closer to: a deterministic runtime for governed knowledge state, authority, evidence, lifecycle and provenance'; Position B (20260821-2351, P2, 23:51, same evening, 3h19m later) rates the Unix/Linux analogy as weak because 'knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution, strict process isolation, universal semantics.' A possible reconciliation (governance-determinism vs. execution-determinism) is explicitly NOT accepted since neither document draws the distinction; v1.1's silence on determinism leaves workbook item W:C-2 (determinism: property, test, or DEF-1?) open and unruled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Research suggests the trustworthy core of organizational knowledge is primarily about preserving epistemic accountability over time, not retrieval performance.
b_rows_sample.statement: The external review explicitly excludes RAG, ontologies, workflow engines, analytics, visualization, and event sourcing from the trustworthy core, and rates knowledge graphs as Strong for integration/query/semantic model but Weak as Kernel and Mixed as persistence ('no evidence supports Knowledge System = Knowledge Graph'). Framed as a third independent arrival (with S1-F001's 0/20 authority-validity measurement and the Phase 2 temporal thread) at 'over time' as the load-bearing dimension, and as largely agreeing with two other independent rejection sets (KCON-016; v1.1 §17).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The artifact in hand is not the persistence record. It is a Phase-1 narrative document, located in `brainstorming/`, that *describes* measurements over persistence records.
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F001 assigns its source the strongest evidence class in the corpus ('implementation/persistence-derived evidence — priority 1-3, not priority-7 brainstorming'), but the cited document (brainstorming/20260821-2033-what-eks-is-today.md) is a brainstorming-corpus narrative describing measurements, not the persistence record itself, and no grant identifier, record path, or query is quoted — the measurement is asserted, not exhibited. Proposed remedy: record as 'secondary report of persistence-derived measurement', mark underlying grants verifiable-on-request rather than verified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is an **implemented** mechanism, not a proposal — evidence priority 1–3, not 7.
b_rows_sample.statement: The same one-band evidence-class elevation recurs in S1-F003's ChangeSet claim ('an implemented mechanism, not a proposal') with no code path, module, test or commit cited; two instances from the same corpus location, both elevating, make this a pattern rather than a single slip — a systematic upward bias that is harder to detect than one misclassification since each instance looks locally reasonable. Explicitly does not doubt either substantive claim (S1-F001's 0/20 grants or S1-F003's ChangeSet), only their evidence-class labeling.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest set of genuinely irreducible epistemic capabilities required for KnowledgeOS to support the required knowledge lifecycle? ... This is a MINIMALITY / ABLATION experiment. It is NOT a naming exercise.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the primary research question as a formal ablation experiment over candidate operator set C0 (13 operators), explicitly distinguishing it from naming exercises, aesthetic simplification, universal-necessity claims, or retrofitting existing architecture, and requiring provenance tagging ([CORPUS]/[EXT]/[INF]/[PROP]/[EXP]/[NEG]/[OPEN]) with no silent promotion to canon.

a_rows_sample.anchor: if the proposed implementation merely changes Discriminate into DiscriminateIncludingGapDetection, then DetectGap has NOT actually been eliminated. That is semantic smuggling.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines 'semantic smuggling' as the critical failure mode of the whole experiment: claiming an operator is reducible by silently renaming its function into a remaining operator (e.g. Remove DetectGap, redefine Validate to also detect gaps) rather than genuinely composing it from independent semantics -- requires an explicit SMUGGLING=TRUE/FALSE flag with justification for every proposed reduction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Cardinality minimality ... B. Semantic minimality ... C. Compositional minimality ... D. Architectural minimality ... E. Cognitive universality. Do NOT assume these are equivalent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five non-equivalent senses of kernel 'minimality' (cardinality; semantic -- no operator removable without losing an irreducible capability; compositional -- every retained operator contributes something non-reproducible by composition of others; architectural -- no separate responsibility introduced when naturally derivable from another; cognitive universality -- required by every epistemic system), designating semantic+compositional minimality as the primary experimental target and cardinality as only secondary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C1 acquire an observation ... C24 support learning from new observations. These are INITIAL capabilities. ... Do not optimize the capability list merely to make the operator set smaller.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 24-item capability space (C1-C24, spanning observation acquisition, meaning construction, representation, relation, discrimination, hypothesis formation, inference, gap detection, challenge, validation, revision, inquiry-adequacy determination, action selection, context/temporal/uncertainty/assumption representation, provenance and alternative preservation, non-identifiability support, observation-vs-interpretation distinction, representation-independent semantic equivalence, smallest-adequate-answer production, and learning from new observations) that must be derived independently of the candidate operator names, not by restating them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: oi : S_i -> S_j where S_i and S_j are abstract epistemic states/artifacts. Do not assume all operators act directly on K_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes candidate operators as typed transformations over explicitly distinct carrier types (Observation, Evidence, SemanticRepresentation, Hypothesis, Model, Claim, AlternativeSet, RequirementSet, EpistemicState, DecisionProposal), explicitly rejecting the assumption that every operator acts directly on K_t, and requires every proposed composite reduction o_removed=f(o_remaining) to be documented across nine dimensions (input/output type, preconditions, postconditions, semantic/epistemic effect, information loss, introduced assumptions, and whether removed semantics were secretly embedded elsewhere).

a_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO 7 — Missing evidence ... Expected possibility: cannot determine. ... SCENARIO 12 — Smallest adequate answer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a 16-scenario canonical test suite grounded in concrete Nexus-infrastructure examples (basic/numeric/network observation; conflicting evidence; ambiguous semantics like 'the server is available'; temporal revision without conflating historical and current-state equality; missing evidence legitimately yielding 'cannot determine'; competing partially-supported hypotheses; model criticism; context-dependent semantic interpretation; inquiry-relative adequacy; smallest adequate answer; cost-constrained action selection; non-identifiability; provenance conflict; representation equivalence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Build a SMALL RESEARCH SIMULATOR. ... Do NOT claim this is the canonical KnowledgeOS state model. Label it: [PROP] experimental state representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires building a small, explicitly non-production research simulator over an explicitly [PROP]-labelled experimental epistemic state K_t=(claims,representations,relations,evidence,provenance,assumptions,alternatives,uncertainty,context,history), with every helper function classified (domain operator / data-structure operation / infrastructure utility / test harness / serialization) so that only genuine domain operators count toward kernel size.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Leave-one-out is not sufficient. Some operators may be individually removable but jointly necessary. ... pairwise ablation; ... selected triple ablations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires pairwise and higher-order ablation beyond simple leave-one-out, explicitly anticipating that some operators may be individually removable yet jointly necessary (synergy, substitution, hidden dependency, or operator bundles) -- illustrated by Interpret+Represent potentially being coupled without necessarily being one operator, requiring a typed factorization test rather than an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROPERTY P2 — Non-identifiability: If evidence cannot distinguish H1 and H2, the system must not fabricate a unique determination. ... PROPERTY P7 — No information creation: Processing existing evidence cannot create unsupported empirical information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ten falsifiable properties (P1-P10) for randomized property-based simulation testing: revision-representability under contradicting evidence, non-fabrication under non-identifiability, provenance preservation, temporal consistency (no erasure of historical truth), semantic distinction preserved when evidence does not resolve it, adequacy != mere answer-existence, no information creation from pure processing, alternative preservation absent evidence-based elimination, context-sensitivity of relevance, and challenge-required-before-validated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT interpret a 99% scenario success rate as proof of correctness. ... Statistics support robustness assessment; they do not prove minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes disciplined statistical treatment: separate deterministic logical failures from stochastic/implementation/model-specification/conceptual failures, report failure rates and robustness across seeds and sensitivity to definitional choices rather than a single aggregate score, and explicitly distinguishes the statistical robustness question (p_hat_failure) from the logical necessity question (exists x: Reach(S,x) != Reach(S union {o},x)) -- statistics inform robustness, they do not establish minimality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But do NOT equate: information quantity = knowledge. ... Do NOT equate: Pi_t = K_t. ... fit != validation, regression != causality, estimation != identification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the experiment to run information-theoretic checks (data-processing inequality, sufficient representation) without equating information quantity with knowledge, probabilistic checks (Pi_t=L(X|F_t) without Pi_t=K_t) across six specified uncertainty scenarios, and a causal/model-criticism check enforcing fit!=validation, regression!=causality, estimation!=identification as three explicitly distinct failure classes a model must not conflate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = predicate ... Ideal State = state/target construct ... Inquiry = domain input ... Governance = external constraint ... Authorization = governance mechanism ... Select = decision/action mechanism. But these are hypotheses. Test them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a DDD pass over every candidate operator asking whether it is a genuine domain capability owning a distinct invariant/responsibility, or instead a policy, state predicate, or orchestration concern -- explicitly naming Zero, Ideal State, Inquiry, Governance, Authorization, and Select as operators whose kernel membership must be tested rather than assumed, offering (only as hypotheses) demotions of each to a non-operator role.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not conclude: 'Operator X is necessary because the current KnowledgeOS architecture already has X.' That would be circular.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids architectural circularity as a justification for kernel membership (existing class != domain primitive; existing service != kernel operator; existing workflow != epistemic necessity), requiring the experiment to reason from domain capabilities and epistemic requirements rather than from current implementation structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 — Representation failure ... F19 — Implementation artifact ... F20 — Simulator artifact. Do not call F19/F20 kernel failures. ... Never manufacture a positive result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a twenty-category failure taxonomy (F1-F20) for classifying ablation failures, explicitly excluding implementation and simulator artifacts (F19/F20) from counting as genuine kernel failures, and mandates that negative results ('removing X did not break anything', 'no meaningful conclusion can currently be drawn') be treated as first-class, valid, and never suppressed in favor of manufactured positive findings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Search for multiple Pareto candidates. ... Do not collapse these into one arbitrary weighted score.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires searching for multiple Pareto-optimal candidate kernels (not one single smallest kernel) evaluated along nine uncollapsed axes (cardinality, semantic coverage, compositionality, coupling, interpretability, falsifiability, domain cohesion, implementation independence, evidence strength), with any weighted composite score requiring an explicit sensitivity analysis over weight choices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: find S subset-of O such that C_required subset-of Reach(S) and forall o in S: C_required not-subset-of Reach(S \ {o}). ... Reach(S) ... must be defined carefully.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes semantic minimality as a set-system reachability problem: find a minimal operator subset S such that all required capabilities are reachable by valid typed compositions of S, and no operator in S can be removed without breaking that containment -- explicitly cautioning that the Reach(S) composition function must be defined by explicit, non-arbitrary rules rather than declared to include whatever the researcher wishes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Empirically necessary ... Formally necessary ... DDD-necessary ... These can disagree. ... That is a very interesting result -- not a contradiction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three independent necessity tests (empirical: the simulator cannot run without it; formal: no valid composition of remaining operators supplies it; DDD: the responsibility is a genuinely distinct domain concept) that can legitimately disagree without contradiction, illustrated by Select potentially being computationally derivable from Determine while DDD analysis still separates epistemic determination from action selection as distinct responsibilities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 01-research-question.md ... 03-capability-model.md ... 04-operator-contracts.md ... 05-operator-capability-matrix.md ... 06-composition-rules.md ... FINAL-kernel-reduction-report.md
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes a fixed 18-file experimental output directory (docs/knowledgeos/research/kernel-reduction/), explicitly forbidding modification of canonical architecture documents and requiring the simulator code to be isolated in an experimental directory -- this file naming scheme directly matches several files this same batch reads (01-research-question.md, 03-capability-model.md, 04-operator-contracts.md, 05-operator-capability-matrix.md, 06-composition-rules.md), identifying this prompt as their likely originating mandate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would consider the experiment successful even if Claude concludes: 'The 13 operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because the semantic granularity of the candidate operators is unstable.' ... What is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive?
a_rows_sample.statement: Names as potentially the single most valuable possible experimental outcome a finding that the 13 candidate operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because their semantic granularity is itself unstable -- reframing the open research problem from 'which operator to delete' to 'what is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive', and explicitly allows the kernel to turn out structurally different from a flat operator set (e.g. K=(S,T,O) or K=(P,R,delta), or some operators turning out to be predicates like Zero rather than transformations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4. The operation-necessity test: a test was run -- but not the one G-67 names ... exhaustive search over all 16384 subsets ... minimal kernels: exactly two, both cardinality 13 ... under every audit reduction granted, |K_min| falls 13 -> 8 ... But the headline is self-superseded: Reachability != Epistemic adequacy ... PARTIALLY MOVED. An ablation ran, and it measured a different quantity than G-67 asks for. R_mandatory was never the input -- a 25-capability model was. ... AF-F-33 stays withdrawn and is now superseded by measured numbers from a declared model. 13 and 8 are not upgrades of my 14/18.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports an executed 16384-subset kernel-reduction ablation (KR-2026-09-01) as PARTIALLY MOVING the lane's operation-necessity question: it is a genuine, careful experiment (finding two minimal 13-operator kernels, a missing Qualify power, |K_min| falling to 8 under every granted audit reduction, and 7/7 semantic-smuggling probes rejected), but it measures a different quantity than the lane's own G-67 criterion (which requires R_mandatory as input; the ablation instead used a declared 25-capability model) -- so the lane's prior withdrawal of AF-F-33 (its 14-forced/18-upper-bound claim) stays withdrawn and correct, and 13/8 are explicitly not upgrades of 14/18 since the two questions ('minimal under this capability model and algebra' vs 'forced by R_mandatory') remain distinct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the headline is self-superseded (19-directive-adoption-and-research-restructure.md): Reachability != Epistemic adequacy. 'The experiment falsified the assumption that kernel minimality can be determined independently of semantic representation.' The programme sequence becomes Representation -> Capability -> Reachability -> Minimality, and the kernel question moves from first to seventh in a seven-level hierarchy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the kernel-reduction ablation's own follow-up document self-supersedes its headline result by falsifying the assumption that kernel minimality can be determined independently of semantic representation (Reachability != Epistemic adequacy), restructuring the whole research programme sequence to Representation -> Capability -> Reachability -> Minimality and demoting the kernel-minimality question from first to seventh position in a seven-level research hierarchy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can two independent engineers implement the same kernel from the current material, without the research corpus? STILL NO. But the reason changed, and the change is the finding: [table of 5 blockers, 2026-08-31 vs 2026-09-02] The blockers moved DOWNWARD -- from vocabulary disagreement to semantic undefinedness. A vocabulary blocker is resolved by a governance act; a semantic blocker is resolved by a derivation. The estate has traded four governance blockers for four derivation blockers.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the central implementability readiness question (can two independent engineers implement the same kernel from current material without the research corpus?) as STILL NO, but frames the change as progress: five specific blockers are named across the 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02 snapshots, and the overall shift is that blockers moved from vocabulary disagreement (resolvable by a governance act) to semantic undefinedness (resolvable only by a derivation) -- summarized as 'the estate has traded four governance blockers for four derivation blockers', explicitly framed as real progress since derivation blockers are the kind a research lane can actually discharge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lane-summary changes: Formal definition exists 25/25 unchanged; Executable test exists 22/25 -> 23/25 (O_core minimality now has an executable test of a different criterion; the G-67 criterion still has none); Architecture 1/25 re-measured unchanged; Governance 1/25 unchanged, four [RATIFIED] stamps and two [DECIDED] records not locatable; Zero remaining blocker 4/25 unchanged (Equality's reason now worse: 9 registers, not 4); Operations 0/25; Transformations 0/25. Not one construct moved from BLOCKED to unblocked. The architecture and governance counts did not move at all.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the full seven-row lane-summary delta table for the 25-construct readiness matrix, confirming only one of seven summary counts moved at all (Executable-test-exists 22/25 -> 23/25, for a criterion different from the one originally posed), while Architecture and Governance both remain frozen at 1/25; closes with the boxed summary: not one construct moved from BLOCKED to unblocked, and the architecture and governance counts did not move at all across this entire window.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the real ownership map is the space map
a_rows_sample.statement: Where ownership DOES change, the boundary is a SPACE, not a viewpoint: platform (DA) -> EKP (nab.raj.sharma) -> product (the producing track). This claim is downgraded from finding to hypothesis in REV 2 because it was observed on one platform instance only; generalizing it as an architectural property requires KnowledgeOS applied elsewhere (the second-adopter gate).

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-VO-4 | Whether space-ownership (platform/EKP/product) is the platform's REAL context map
a_rows_sample.statement: Unknown U-VO-4: whether space-ownership (platform/EKP/product) is the platform's real context map — the strongest candidate reading of Finding 1 — deliberately left as a strategic-DDD question for humans, not answered by the author.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R-4 | Space —generates→ Projection —attested→ authoritative | HIGH
a_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-4: Space generates Projection, attested to become authoritative. External support: CQRS (read models rebuildable, non-authoritative) plus audit/signature practice and data-product certification. No challenge — the corrected form IS the standard model. Confidence: HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R-9 | Knowledge Space —declared boundary→; spaces NEST | MEDIUM-HIGH
a_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-9: a Knowledge Space has a declared boundary and spaces nest (deployment = nested space). External support: bounded contexts (CANONICAL), data-mesh domains (boundary+owner). Challenge: nesting is less standardized than bounding. Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH overall (boundary HIGH, nesting MEDIUM).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Space = declared boundary + owner + constitution ... bounded contexts (Evans) · data-mesh domain ownership · SKOS
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Space as declared boundary + owner + constitution is supported by bounded contexts (Evans), data-mesh domain ownership, and SKOS concept schemes. Confidence: HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
a_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

a_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — review 2026-08-03 (1420), three amendments annotated, none rewritten
a_rows_sample.statement: Three amendments: (1) the 'nine kinds' are held as candidate archetypes, not frozen primitives, until MM-1 resolves whether KIND is itself a dimension; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE, since its distinguishing edge ('generates Projections') is observed in only one space (the EKP) and nesting is unevidenced (H-3); (3) PURPOSE is flagged for its own investigation (U-MM-4, waits on D-5).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kinds the candidates missed but the passes repeatedly found: PURPOSE · CONTAINER · PROJECTION
a_rows_sample.statement: Three additional kinds were repeatedly found by the passes but missing from the A-G candidate list: PURPOSE (mission/vision, found twice in the Relationship Ontology), CONTAINER (Knowledge Space — declared boundary, nesting), and PROJECTION (derived, operating in production).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Classification — every gap from the projection ... G-1..G-5
a_rows_sample.statement: Five gaps classified by category (Structural/Behavioral/Evolutionary) and cause: G-1 (I-4/ATTESTS/PROJECTION inert-vs-attested) is EVOLUTIONARY, caused by a missing lifecycle, belongs to LIFECYCLE. G-2 (SPECIALIZES, Engineering Knowledge -> product knowledge) is EVOLUTIONARY, a missing relationship, belongs to ONTOLOGY. G-3 (external authority/CONSTRAINS) is BEHAVIORAL, a missing relationship (obligation != ownership), belongs to GOVERNANCE. G-4 (PRODUCT vs DEPLOYMENT/INSTANTIATES) is STRUCTURAL but dissolves: a deployment is a nested Knowledge Space, so it belongs to ONTOLOGY as resolved, no new concept. G-5 (Runtime Adapter disappeared in both new domains) is STRUCTURAL but is a confirmation of Hexagonal behaving correctly, not a failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-4 answers H-3 — the nesting question — using evidence rather than preference: Knowledge Spaces NEST, and a deployment is the nested case
a_rows_sample.statement: H-3 (the nesting question) is answered by G-4: Knowledge Spaces nest, and a deployment is the nested case. No new concept was introduced; the ontology already explained the evidence, which is the test the commission set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
a_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
a_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ANNOTATED 2026-08-02 — THREE CORRECTIONS ... LEVEL MIXING — my third instance of that error class
a_rows_sample.statement: Three annotated corrections (recorded in KnowledgeOS_Relationship_Ontology.md): (1) section 2's six concepts are not siblings but four ontological layers (Purpose/Mission, Platform/Capability+Knowledge, Representation/Artifact, Application/PKS+Product) listed as one set — a third instance of level mixing; (2) PKS is a CONTAINER, not a layer below ARTIFACT — a PKS contains artifacts, and KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted as the container concept, defined by a declared boundary (scope.include), not a folder; (3) the document itself conflates two levels — section 1 (dimensions) is a meta-model, section 2 (concepts) is an ontology, both named rather than the whole renamed. The chain in section 2 is completed by naming DP-n (DESIGN POLICY) as the anchor stopping capabilities from floating, observable in the Capability Catalog's 1:1 CAP->DP binding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
a_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE — admitted, and the evidence is a boundary, not a folder ... A Knowledge Space is not a folder. It is a DECLARED SCOPE with an owner and a governing constitution
a_rows_sample.statement: KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted, evidenced by: knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include; three registered documentation roots (knowledgeos, pks, publicdigit); ES-005.1's three concerns (Product, Platform, Runtime mount); the EKP having its own constitution and owner. A Knowledge Space is a declared scope with an owner and a governing constitution, not a folder — which is why the '13% coverage' question was a scope decision, not a bug.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship model — the commission's seven questions ... contains = a container relation · references = a pointer · generates = produces a new instance · depends on = cannot be understood without
a_rows_sample.statement: A full relationship table across all thirteen concepts, using four typed relations (contains = container relation, references = a pointer, generates = produces a new instance, depends on = cannot be understood without). Notable entries: KNOWLEDGE SPACE may contain artifacts and other knowledge spaces, generates PROJECTIONS; PKS may contain product artifacts but never reusable Method, references Engineering Knowledge, generates Product Projections; ARTIFACT is a leaf (contains nothing) but depends on the Knowledge it represents; KNOWLEDGE generates nothing, being represented rather than generative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Missing concepts — recorded as hypotheses, not admitted (H-1..H-4)
a_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate concepts recorded as hypotheses, none admitted: H-1 'I-12', a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads (n=1 capability, needs a second cross-boundary reader); H-2 Engineering Domain as owner of Capabilities (no artifact binds a CAP to a PD; DP-n already fills the slot); H-3 Knowledge Space nesting, does the EKP contain the PKS or sit beside it (containment vs adjacency unevidenced); H-4 whether OPERATIONAL-STATE attaches to the Artifact or the Knowledge it carries (would change I-1's granularity).

a_rows_sample.anchor: RO-2 | Are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent?
a_rows_sample.statement: RO-2: are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent (H-3) — authority: ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The three challenges — accepted, and one is settled by my own evidence rules ... CONTAINER demoted CONFIRMED → CANDIDATE ... my own admission rule decides it, not deference
a_rows_sample.statement: Three reviewer challenges: (1) 'Archetype' replaces 'nine kinds' until MM-1, since 'archetype' already exists in the corpus (RQ-002) so the rename mints nothing — a ubiquitous-language decision, decided with governance (MM-1), not unilaterally; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE by the author's own admission rule: 'Containers generate Projections' is observed in exactly one space (the EKP's knowledge-graph.php), n=1, and nesting is unevidenced (H-3) — the settling test is a second generating space (confirms) or a capability-plus-scope reduction (refutes); (3) PURPOSE, possibly more fundamental than Container, is flagged not resolved, since the mission is enacted and unratified (D-5 pending), and deepening PURPOSE before ratification would model ahead of the domain expert — recorded as hypothesis U-ONT-2, n=0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What exists instead ... FOUR DISTINCT PARTIAL ORDERS, one per relationship type: AUTHORITY · PRODUCTION · REALIZATION · CONTAINMENT
a_rows_sample.statement: Four evidenced partial orders replace the refuted single stack: AUTHORITY (who justifies whom) PURPOSE->STRATEGY->PRINCIPLE->DP-n->CAPABILITY; PRODUCTION (who produces whom) PROCESS->Knowledge/Artifacts/Evidence, CAPABILITY->Evidence, CONTAINER->Projection (n=1); REALIZATION (concept -> executable/persistent form) KNOWLEDGE->ARTIFACT (I-1), CAPABILITY->RUNTIME ASSET (R-7, SC-6 gap); CONTAINMENT (what moves together) CONTAINER contains Artifacts (contains other spaces? H-3 open). The intuition underneath the stack survives: relations are directional, with DOMAIN/KNOWLEDGE conceptual and RUNTIME/ARTIFACT realized; but 'which is above' is only answerable per relation, not for the stack as a whole.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer proposes a "Provenance Domain" ... Verdict: PROVENANCE is not a missing domain — it is a DISPERSED, NAMED, PARTLY-GOVERNED concern
b_rows_sample.statement: A check-before-recording pass finds provenance already lives in the corpus as: one axis of AUTHORITY itself (provenance x standing, Engineering Progression Model, PM-1), the PROVENANCE non-progression kind, identity discipline (CAP-001), evidence grading practice ([FETCHED]/[CANONICAL]/[2nd-hand]), and append-only evidence/traceability blocks. Verdict: provenance is a dispersed, named, partly-governed concern (the SP-5 pattern recognized a third time), not a missing domain. Disposition: the provenance questions enrich the existing Tier-1 Knowledge Governance stream (PM-1); 'Provenance as a strategic domain' is recorded as a hypothesis routed to the docket, admissible only if a live stream produces evidence requiring it; the identity-chain observation (CAP-001 as foundation if provenance grows) is a watch item, not a promotion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-GR-2 | Provenance: enrichment of Knowledge Governance (current disposition) or eventually its own domain?
b_rows_sample.statement: U-GR-2: whether provenance remains an enrichment of Knowledge Governance or eventually becomes its own domain, waiting on operational evidence from the live streams, not literature.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-1 ENRICHED (2026-08-03, external input): PROVENANCE as a named first-class concern
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-1 (provenance x standing) is enriched: industry treats provenance as a governance control plane (identity -> version -> retrieval event -> evidence -> answer -> audit), paralleling P4 and resting on identity discipline (CAP-001). Provenance already lives dispersed in the corpus (authority axis, non-progression kind, evidence grading, traceability blocks); 'Provenance as its own domain' is a hypothesis at the docket, not a new backlog stream — this row owns the questions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: authority = provenance × standing ... [CANONICAL] W3C PROV: derivation is an immutable provenance fact
b_rows_sample.statement: The formula authority = provenance x standing is supported by W3C PROV (derivation is an immutable provenance fact) and data-catalog practice (lineage != 'certified' flag are two independent fields in every major catalog). No challenge. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SC-5 | authority = provenance × standing in ONE field (its own header asks two questions)
b_rows_sample.statement: SC-5: authority combines provenance and standing into one field, though its own header asks two separate questions; open, routed to PM-1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED IN FULL — AND IT IS MY FOURTH INSTANCE OF LEVEL CONFUSION ... I-4 is NOT falsified. I misdiagnosed a LIFECYCLE gap as an ONTOLOGY falsification
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior claim that I-4 was falsified is retracted: a discharge summary is not authoritative because it was projected, but became authoritative through DERIVED -> REVIEWED -> ATTESTED -> RELEASED; governance created the authority, not the derivation. The corrected conclusion is not 'DP-2 is wrong' but 'DP-2 conflates DERIVATION with ATTESTATION'. Four prior level confusions listed: flat vs dimensional (taxonomy), artifact vs concept (existence), layer vs sibling (ontology), lifecycle vs structure (this one). A fifth was avoided by checking: the author was about to report 'there is no lifecycle', when in fact nine exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The precise gap — located mechanically ... THE GAP: STATUS HAS A GOVERNED STATE MACHINE. AUTHORITY DOES NOT
b_rows_sample.statement: statuses.yaml and authorities.yaml are declared orthogonal but are not equally equipped: statuses.yaml has 8 values, a progression field (order), a terminal marker (settled), a defined who-may-move role table, and lint-checkable transition guards; authorities.yaml has 5 values and none of these. Authority gates a status transition, but nothing governs how authority itself changes — no rule for who may move derived->authoritative, and no guard for it. This is exactly the I-4 problem: attestation is an authority transition (derived->authoritative); because authority transitions are ungoverned, the model cannot express 'attested', so it collapses derived into 'never authoritative'. A prior reviewer's diagnosis ('DP-2 conflates derivation and attestation') now has a mechanical cause.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 (WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 — ILL-POSED) ... authority is TWO dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE × act-changed STANDING
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') is withdrawn as ill-posed: the question dissolved under discovery that authority is two dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE (generated, derived) times act-changed STANDING (authoritative, provisional, historical). Provenance cannot have a state machine; standing changes by governance acts. Superseded by PM-1/PM-2, recorded in the Engineering Progression Model section 4.

b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve conclusions reproduced blind, now carrying double independent derivation: (1) KnowledgeOS is a hypothesis, gate shut, Vision unapproved; (2) 'PublicDigit is the laboratory' rejected against ADR-AIP-02, Product Primacy governs; (3) the EKP is a real governed context with named individual owner; (4) Engineering Governance is the strongest bounded context; (5) the reusable kernel list, near-identical; (6) designed-for-reuse != demonstrated-reusable (verbatim convergence); (7) individual EKP ownership is a succession risk, sharpened to 'separation of duties is real as process and unevidenced as people'; (8) three knowledge ontologies coexist unreconciled; (9) domain-free methodology sits in product paths, placement breached, plus a new instance (Platform_Capability_Pattern); (10) PMR-10's manual adoption failed, sharpened into a falsification of the Reference Architecture's protocol-suffices stance; (11) most of the 11 invariants reproduced with citations, with I-8 downgraded to invariant-in-waiting; (12) the split verdict itself (enacted internal mission vs unratified product vision).
