a_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion contains a proposition. That does not mean P subset A. ... Containment \neq Set Inclusion ... P \xrightarrow{embedded in} A \xrightarrow{member of} K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the K_P subset K_A subset K_J subset K_t subset Omega chain as a category error: propositions, assertions and knowledge states are different types of object, and containment (a proposition being embedded in an assertion) is not the same relation as set inclusion (an assertion being a member of a knowledge state's assertion set); replaces it with a typed composition chain (embedded-in / member-of / subset-of).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Instead of A=(P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi), use Supports(E,A) or EvidenceRelation(E,A,r) where r in {supports,contradicts,qualifies,weakens,contextualizes}
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes moving Evidence out of the Assertion tuple into an explicit typed relation (Supports/Contradicts/Qualifies/Weakens/Contextualizes between Evidence and Assertion) rather than embedding it as a field, since one assertion may be supported or contradicted by several distinct evidence items with different relation types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero and Lord should not be components of Knowledge... Zero is an operation: Zero: K -> Z. Lord is an operation: Lord: K -> L.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms and generalizes the earlier circularity concern (from S0784): Zero and Lord must be typed as operations Zero:K->Z and Lord:K->L over the Knowledge State type K, never as stored fields of K itself; their outputs may be persisted as derived artifacts but are not foundational components of knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity | Dimension | Value | Proposition | Evidence | Epistemic State | Assertion | Relationship | Knowledge State | Knowledge Space ... a type system defines: what kinds of objects exist, what properties each has, how types relate, what operations are valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Answers the posed Question 7A by producing a complete ten-type system for KnowledgeOS (Entity, Dimension, Value, Proposition, Evidence, EpistemicState, Assertion, Relationship, KnowledgeState, KnowledgeSpace) with formal set-builder definitions, a type hierarchy diagram, per-type well-formedness constraints, and operation signatures (Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Compare/Challenge/Update/Preserve, all typed as maps between these object types).

a_rows_sample.anchor: WellTyped(K) = WellTypedObjects(K) and WellTypedRelationships(K) and ValidCardinalities(K) ... Supports(Evidence,Assertion) valid; Supports(Person,Assertion) invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects WellTyped from a pure object-typing predicate to also require relationship typing and cardinality validity (e.g. Supports must relate Evidence to Assertion, not Person to Assertion), since syntactically valid objects can still violate relationship-type rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U = {E, D, V, P, A, R, E_v, Sigma, H, Z, L, K, I} ... this ontology is the foundation for all KnowledgeOS operations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 13-type universe (Entity, Dimension, Value, Proposition, Assertion, Relationship, Evidence, EpistemicState, History, ZeroFinding, LordCandidate, KnowledgeState, IdealState) with formal set-builder definitions, well-formedness predicates for Proposition/Assertion/Relationship, and an explicit epistemic lattice claim over the 2240-state Sigma space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: You later define Relationship separately... Relationship in Entity and Relationship in Relationship could become possible. Entity != Relationship.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Entity definition (which included 'relationship' as an example subject) for creating an ontological ambiguity where a Relationship could also be typed as an Entity; a relationship may become the subject of a proposition without itself being classified as an Entity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P=(E,D,V) ... too restrictive for the complete KnowledgeOS theory ... doesn't naturally represent 'Bhishma supports the Kaurava side' or 'Assertion A contradicts Assertion B' or 'Evidence E supports Assertion A' ... P=(S,rho,O,Gamma) ... AttributeProposition subset Proposition
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Entity+Dimension+Value proposition model as too narrow to represent relational/meta propositions (assertion-contradicts-assertion, evidence-supports-assertion); generalizes Proposition to a subject-predicate-object-qualifiers form P=(S,rho,O,Gamma), with the earlier attribute proposition recovered as the special case rho=hasDimension, so AttributeProposition becomes a subtype of Proposition rather than the whole of it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: To call something a lattice mathematically, you need a partial order such that every pair has lub and glb. You haven't defined that... Replace Transition Lattice with Epistemic State Space or Epistemic Transition System.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the claim that the epistemic state space (Sigma=A x S x R x V x C with a proposed preceq order) forms a mathematical lattice, since the required least-upper-bound/greatest-lower-bound structure was never established and the Resolution component (Open/InProgress/Resolved/Unresolvable) is not naturally ordered; downgrades the claim to an unstructured product state space pending proof of any lattice properties.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(E_v,P) in [-1,1] ... epistemically dangerous... I recommend replacing the primitive scalar with Bearing(E,P) in {Support,Contradict,Neutral,Irrelevant,Unknown} and separately Strength(E,P) in [0,1].
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the signed [-1,1] evidence-support scalar (0 could mean neutral, irrelevant, insufficient, unknown, or not-assessed -- these are not equivalent), replacing it with a categorical Bearing (Support/Contradict/Neutral/Irrelevant/Unknown) plus an optional separate numeric Strength.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An Assertion without evidence must be representable, otherwise Zero cannot represent a missing-evidence condition... Evidence(A) subseteq E_v and |Evidence(A)| >= 0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Assertion well-formedness rule that required a non-empty Evidence field, which would make MissingEvidence (an established Gap type) unrepresentable; an assertion's Evidence set must be allowed to be empty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: You use ~ for both Consistent (line 480) and Normative Conflict (line 488). That is unacceptable in a formal theory... A1 => A2 as causal... but => is conventionally logical implication. Causation != LogicalEntailment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags an actual notation error (the symbol ~ used for two different relationship types, Consistent and Normative Conflict, in the same table) and a symbol-overload error (=> used for causal implication when it conventionally denotes logical implication), recommending distinct notations and the explicit invariant Causation != LogicalEntailment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Content != EpistemicStatus != Evaluation ... Ontology -> Formal Semantics -> State Model -> Evaluation Algebra -> DDD Model -> Implementation, not Graph Schema -> Call it Ontology.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the batch's summary methodological principle: Content, Epistemic Status, and Evaluation are three different mathematical objects that must never be collapsed, and warns against letting a convenient implementation/graph-database representation silently substitute for genuine formal ontology work (Ontology->Semantics->StateModel->EvaluationAlgebra->DDD->Implementation, never the reverse).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
=> Of 10 propositions the corpus itself requires, 2 are cleanly expressible.
     THREE are inexpressible
b_rows_sample.statement: EXP-19: tested against 10 propositions the corpus itself states it needs to express, P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) cleanly expresses only 2; 3 are inexpressible (negation — no negative values in V_D; conditional — 'IF v>=3.60 THEN patch-current', the founding conditional-determination problem; universal quantification — 'every committee has >=3 members'); 2 are lossy (a validity interval collapses to one timestamp t; a unit is dropped); 1 ('A1 contradicts A2') is not a proposition at all in this type system and must be expressed as an R-edge instead, giving the theory two uncoordinated mechanisms for propositional content; 1 ('Nexus is ready to migrate') is expressible but empty, holding the conclusion with no way to express the rule that produced it; 1 ('Nexus.version is UNKNOWN') is ambiguous between a value-space category error and true absence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### 2.1 `P = (E,D,V)` — **the corpus refutes it in the same file that supplies it**
b_rows_sample.statement: Divergence 1: Q14 (20260826-182409) supplies P=(E,D,V) and then, in its own §3 titled 'The biggest mathematical problem: Proposition = Entity + Dimension + Value', calls it too restrictive and recommends P=(S,ρ,O,Γ) as 'a very important correction' — never adopted (AttributeProposition occurs in exactly one file); Step 262 reopens it and records it as an open sub-test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | 6 | Can evidence exist without an assertion? | 🟡 **type-yes, semantically-no** |
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest of nine mandated counterexamples: E_q is indexed by the claim q it is evidence for (Step 230.15), but the theory's amended 9-field evidence record drops this index, making evidence free-floating; this loses both the ability to say what an item is evidence for, and the domain the independence relation (needed for corroboration) would need to live on.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Golden Trace: Decision→Policy→Rule→Context→Agent→Recommendation→Authorization→Action→Evidence→Verification→Finding→Disposition. Trace(A)=Reconstruct(Decision,Context,Recommendation,Authorization,Action,Evidence,Verification).
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the 'Golden Trace' as the canonical demonstration artifact against which every implementation phase can be tested, with the reconstructability invariant that a successful golden trace must be reconstructable from stored state alone (no dependence on an LLM's conversational memory necessary); converts this into an architecture fitness rule 'every material governed agent action must have a reconstructable golden trace,' formalized as ArchitectureFitness=Check(GoldenTraceCompleteness).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not replace KnowledgeOS. Evolve it. One Golden Trace. Nexus.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 144 verdict: the concrete evolution strategy is not a platform-wide rewrite but one Golden Trace for one real engineering scenario, with Nexus as the best currently identified reference scenario because it crosses infrastructure, architecture, governance, evidence, assurance, and agent-assisted engineering.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The exact scenario, actors, bounded contexts, input state, commands, domain events, evidence, graph relationships, authorization points, verification rules, expected outputs, failure paths, audit reconstruction, architecture fitness criteria.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 145 (The Golden Trace Specification): defines the Golden Trace as an actual architectural specification (not just a diagram) covering fourteen elements, to produce the first executable KnowledgeOS reference architecture against which Claude, Codex, and the existing EKS mechanisms can be tested.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GT-NEXUS-001: Human, Agent, KnowledgeOS, Governance, Engineering system, Assurance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the reference scenario GT-NEXUS-001 ('an agent must determine whether a planned engineering change to Nexus can proceed under the applicable governance and technical constraints,' analysis/read-only-verification only, no production mutation) and its six logical actors (Human, Agent, KnowledgeOS, Governance, Engineering system, Assurance) with their responsibilities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision D-001, Policy P-001, Rule R-001, Subject NEXUS-001 — all with stable identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the Golden Trace initial state: Decision (status=EFFECTIVE, scope=Nexus, validFrom=T1, authority=Architecture Governance), Knowledge about Nexus (identity, environment, version, repository configuration, infrastructure references, known constraints, each claim with provenance), and Rule R-001 (appliesTo, expected condition, severity, checker, version) as 'an addressable assurance object,' not merely a paragraph of text.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TaskRequest → GetGovernedContext → ContextPackage CTX-001.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks through the agent request (TaskRequest with task/subject/scope/actor/requested operation=ASSESS) and context construction (agent requests GetGovernedContext rather than assembling context itself; Context Service retrieves applicable decisions, relevant claims, applicable rules/findings, current evidence, and agent permissions, producing ContextPackage CTX-001 with ContextVersion=V1).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation REC-001: 'the change appears permissible, subject to verification...' — a recommendation, not a governance decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the agent's first recommendation with schema (agent, session, context, reasoning reference, proposed action, timestamp), explicitly noting the exact storage of chain-of-thought is not prescribed — only decision/provenance metadata is required, not necessarily private internal reasoning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verify(R-001): Assurance → Checker → Nexus Adapter → Nexus → Observation (version=X, observedAt=T2). Observation is not automatically knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks through verification request/checker execution/observation, creating Evidence E-001 (source, subject, observedAt, capturedBy, externalReference, integrity metadata), then Verification V-001 comparing Expected(R-001) against Observed(E-001) with schema (rule, ruleVersion, checkerVersion, subject, evidence, executionTime, verdict) and three possible verdicts PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule=R-001, Evidence=insufficient, Verdict=UNKNOWN, Reason=source unavailable — different from both PASS and FAIL.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked UNKNOWN-verdict example (Nexus unreachable), reinforcing UNKNOWN as a distinct, explicitly supported state; agent's second recommendation after receiving the verification result ('current evidence supports proceeding with the planned assessment, but production execution remains subject to required approval'), restating Recommendation ≠ Authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ActionRequest A-001 = ReadNexusConfiguration (deliberately low-risk). Authorization AUTH-001 evaluated from Agent+Human delegation+Action+Subject+Environment+Policy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first Golden Trace action request as a deliberately low-risk read-only operation and the authorization schema (decision=ALLOW, actor, action, scope, authority, validity, conditions) — more than a boolean.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authorized Action → Nexus Adapter → Nexus. ExecutionID EX-001 → EvidenceID E-002. E-002 → Rule → Verification V-002 — actions themselves can produce assurance evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks through action execution and second-round verification, then the finding/disposition path if V-002=FAIL: Finding F-001 (verification, rule, subject, severity, evidence, status=OPEN) routed to Governance Review yielding disposition REMEDIATE/EXCEPTION/RISK ACCEPTED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-001→P-001→R-001→CTX-001→REC-001→A-001→AUTH-001→EX-001→E-002→V-002→{PASS→Completed, FAIL→F-001→Governance→Disposition}
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the complete Golden Trace as one semantic chain — 'the first complete semantic trace' — and its graph representation with fourteen named edges (governs, establishes, appliesTo, verifiedBy, supportedBy, contains, basedOn, requestedBy, authorizedBy, executedAs, produced, evaluatedBy, raises), concluding 'now the graph has genuine semantic value.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionID, PolicyID, RuleID, SubjectID, ContextID, AgentID, SessionID, RecommendationID, ActionID, AuthorizationID, ExecutionID, EvidenceID, VerificationID, FindingID. TraceID (GT-NEXUS-001) ≠ ActionID ≠ EvidenceID.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the fourteen-item minimum identity set the model must support (not every workflow requires every one) and introduces TraceID as a correlation identifier distinct from any entity ID — the trace represents the workflow, entities represent operations inside it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ContextRequested, ContextProvided, RecommendationCreated, ..., DispositionRecorded — an operational history that does not require full event sourcing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Represents the trace as a thirteen-event sequence, explicitly not requiring full event sourcing — only that important lifecycle transitions be reconstructable, via state+audit records, domain events, outbox, or event sourcing depending on actual requirements.

a_rows_sample.anchor: createdAt, effectiveAt, observedAt, executedAt — not collapsed into one generic timestamp. Knowledge(T2) valid when Action(T4) occurred?
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a four-timestamp temporal model per record and a worked example (Policy effective T1, context T2, observation T3, action T4, verification T5) enabling the question of whether knowledge from T2 was still valid at action time T4; formalizes a temporal-validity precondition (Policy.validAt(T4)?, Authorization.validAt(T4)?, Context.validAt(T4)?) as a deterministic precondition before execution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 Context unavailable, F2 Rule fails, F3 Evidence unavailable, F4 Authorization denied, F5 Execution failure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five named failure paths the reference implementation must demonstrate (not only success): F1 ContextRequest->UNAVAILABLE (with the hard invariant NoContext=>NoExecution for high-risk actions); F2 Verification->FAIL (agent may recommend remediation, but FAIL≠AgentDecision, cannot be overridden); F3 Verification->UNKNOWN (must not be reinterpreted as PASS — platform invariant UNKNOWN≠PASS); F4 ActionRequest->DENY (execution must not occur through the governed path, mechanically enforceable); F5 Authorized->ExecutionFailed (authorization does not imply successful execution, leading to Evidence->Finding/Incident).

a_rows_sample.anchor: GT-001 Action.contextID≠null. GT-002 Action.authorizationID≠null. GT-003..008 covering rule version, evidence-or-UNKNOWN, denied/expired-authorization-cannot-execute, recommendation≠authorization, agent memory not authoritative through use.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines eight trace-level invariants GT-001..GT-008 concretizing the reference architecture: every material action references a context and has authorization; every verification identifies its exact rule version and has evidence or an explicit UNKNOWN reason; a denied or expired authorization cannot execute; agent recommendation ≠ governance authorization; agent memory cannot become authoritative merely through use.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GG-001..005: every verification points to a rule and its evidence; every rule has applicability; every governed action traces to authorization; every finding traces to verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five graph invariants GG-001..GG-005 for the Assurance Graph representation of the trace.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GE-001..005: evidence has source, subject, capture time, provenance; evidence cannot silently change after verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five evidence invariants GE-001..GE-005.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GC-001..005: context is scoped, has identity, has temporal semantics where required, identifies its sources, does not itself become a competing source of truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five context invariants GC-001..GC-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bounded context separation, governed context retrieval, deterministic assurance, agent-independent contracts, complete traceability. Success = 'one real engineering question travels through the complete governed lifecycle without semantic shortcuts.'
b_rows_sample.statement: States the five things the vertical slice must prove simultaneously and its success criterion, distinct from merely 'having a KnowledgeOS application.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assess the current Nexus environment against a defined governance/assurance rule. The actual rule must come from existing governance/assurance material, not be invented for the demo.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the reference use case and insists on grounding it in real existing Nexus/governance material (infrastructure discovery, version info, repos/blob stores, host/container info, network info, migration requirements, known governance questions) rather than synthetic demo data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Excluded from v0.1: production mutation, automatic deployment/migration, complex multi-agent orchestration, full enterprise graph, full event sourcing, microservice decomposition, LLM-based assurance. The slice is Read Only.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first-slice exclusion boundary and presents the first minimal architecture diagram (Claude/Codex->Agent API->Context Service{Governance,Knowledge,Assurance,Evidence}->ContextPackage->Agent->Recommendation->ReadOnly Action->Authorization->Nexus Adapter->Nexus->Observation->Evidence->Deterministic Checker->Verification->Finding/PASS).

b_rows_sample.anchor: knowledgeos/{AGENTS.md, docs/, src/{governance,knowledge,evidence,assurance,agent,action,authorization,context}, adapters/{nexus,git,ci}, infrastructure/, tests/{domain,contract,integration,golden-trace}, .claude/, .codex/}. Agent configuration ≠ Engineering knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate repository structure preserving architectural ownership regardless of technology-specific package layout; restates .claude/.codex hold agent-specific behavior, never becoming the enterprise KnowledgeOS database, with AGENTS.md remaining a pointer/operating contract (repository operating rules, local constraints, how to invoke KnowledgeOS, safety requirements).

b_rows_sample.anchor: First critical path: Context + Evidence + Assurance. Governance v0.1: Decision, Policy, RuleReference, Scope, Validity. Knowledge v0.1: Claim, ClaimStatus, Provenance, EvidenceReferences. Evidence v0.1: EvidenceID, Subject, Source, ObservedAt, Reference, ContentHash, Provenance. Assurance v0.1: Rule, Verification, Verdict, Finding.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies minimal per-module schemas for the first implementation, explicitly not implementing the full enterprise governance lifecycle in the first slice; also gives ContextPackage v0.1 (contextId, traceId, subject, governance, claims, rules, evidence, findings, permissions, provenance) as the most important agent-facing model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GET /context, POST /verifications, GET /verifications/{id}, POST /evidence, POST /recommendations, POST /actions, GET /actions/{id}, POST /authorizations/evaluate — illustrative endpoints; the semantic operations are the architectural contract, not the exact paths.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the minimal first API surface with worked context-request/response JSON examples requiring the response to identify information provenance so the agent never has to guess authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-NEXUS-001: Subject=Nexus, Expected=current state satisfies defined requirement, Checker=NexusStateChecker — grounded in existing material, not invented for architectural convenience.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first deterministic rule and checker contract (Checker{Rule,Subject,Evidence}->Verdict plus structured diagnostics); restates the checker-must-not-use-LLM boundary (f(input)=same output for the same relevant input; the LLM may explain the result but must not decide the authoritative verdict); specifies the first Nexus adapter (read-only NexusPort: getVersion, getRepositories, getBlobStores, getSystemState, only the operations required by the selected rule) translating to a domain-only NexusObservation (no Nexus DTOs leaking into the domain).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus Adapter → Observation → RegisterEvidence → Evidence E42 → (Rule R1 + Evidence E42) → Verification V42. Once complete, V42 must not be rewritten; a later run creates V43.
b_rows_sample.statement: Walks the evidence-registration and verification steps with concrete IDs, restating verification immutability for historical assurance; on FAIL, Finding F42 points back through Verification->Rule->Evidence->Nexus Observation, 'the minimal assurance chain.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation R42 references ContextID, VerificationID, relevant Evidence, TaskID — making it explainable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first Action as READ_ONLY (e.g. READ_NEXUS_CONFIGURATION) so the action/authorization architecture can be tested without operational risk, with even read-only actions passing through ActionRequested->EvaluateAuthorization->ALLOW (simple v0.1 policy, but the architecture must already support the stronger model).

b_rows_sample.anchor: agents, tasks, contexts, decisions, policies, rules, claims, evidence, verifications, findings, recommendations, actions, authorizations, executions, domain_events, outbox, audit_records — following the Aggregate model, not a generic entity/attribute/value schema.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first relational schema and explicitly warns against a generic EAV schema, which destroys type safety, semantic ownership, invariant enforcement, and discoverability despite appearing flexible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Context-contains->Claim, Claim-supportedBy->Evidence, Verification-evaluates->Rule/-uses->Evidence, Finding-causedBy->Verification, Recommendation-basedOn->Context, Action-requestedFrom->Recommendation, Authorization-authorizes->Action, Execution-executes->Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first minimal graph-edge set (achievable via a relational relationship projection, no dedicated graph database needed) and a worked traversal query ('why was this finding raised?': Finding->Verification->Rule->Evidence->Observation->Nexus), 'much more valuable than simply storing a text explanation.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM/EVIDENCE/RULE/FINDING/DECISION/OBSERVATION as distinct search-result types, not 'Nexus — 23 results' — preventing semantic flattening.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first search capability preserving semantic type/authority; specifies the Context Composer v0.1 as explicit per-source queries (getGovernance/getClaims/getRules/getEvidence/getFindings) combined directly, with graph traversal added later for discovery, and explicitly requires the first context path to work even if the graph is unavailable — proving Graph ≠ Authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ContextRequested, ContextProvided, RecommendationCreated, ActionRequested, ActionAuthorized, ActionDenied, ExecutionCompleted, EvidenceRegistered, VerificationCompleted, FindingRaised — do not create dozens of events until actual behavior requires them.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the minimal event vocabulary for v0.1; requires every material domain transition to produce an atomic outbox record; specifies the initial projection consumers (Graph, Search, Trace projections, with Trace Projection especially important for the first Golden Trace); specifies the first audit-record fields (Actor, Operation, Subject, Timestamp, TraceID, CausationID, Result).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claude → KnowledgeOS API → same Context/Rule/Authorization. Codex → KnowledgeOS API → same Context/Rule/Authorization. The domain should not know which agent called it. .claude/.codex/AGENTS.md do not own Governance state; KnowledgeOS owns governed state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the agent-independence symmetry test and the harness-boundary test verifying which components own governance state, directly protecting the previously established architectural principle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Domain: aggregate boundaries implemented, transitions enforced, invalid transitions rejected. API: context/verification/evidence/action-authorization contracts work. Nexus: read-only adapter works, no DTO leakage. Assurance: rule version identified, deterministic checker executes, verification immutable, finding generated on failure. Traceability: TraceID propagated, causation retained, evidence references retained, audit records generated. Agent: Claude and Codex both work via the same contract. Persistence: transactional state persisted, outbox implemented, projections rebuildable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the complete Vertical Slice v0.1 Definition of Done as a checklist across seven categories.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delete all projections; rebuild from authoritative state/events; Graph_rebuilt=Graph_expected and Trace_rebuilt=Trace_expected. Proves projections are not secretly authoritative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the strongest acceptance test — a full projection-deletion-and-rebuild check.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Test A missing evidence → FAIL/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Test B unknown rule version → REJECT. Test C authorization denied → no execution. Test D expired context on high-risk action → BLOCK. Test E duplicate execution request (same ActionID retried) → no unintended duplicate execution.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five named failure-path acceptance tests A-E the vertical slice must deliberately exercise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verify(E,R)=V, repeated Verify(E,R)=V — the result must not change because a different LLM happened to process it. Claude recommendation A vs Codex recommendation B is acceptable variance; Authorization and Verification must remain governed/deterministic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the determinism acceptance test for verification and the agent-nondeterminism boundary distinguishing acceptable reasoning variance from required determinism in authorization/verification, diagrammed as {Claude,Codex}->Reasoning->Recommendation feeding into a deterministic KnowledgeOS control plane {Governance,Assurance,Authorization} — 'the LLM does not disappear, it is simply placed in the correct architectural position.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent assertion (LOW authority): 'I believe Nexus should be upgraded.' Engineering observation (OBSERVATIONAL authority): 'Nexus currently reports version X.' Governed decision (GOVERNANCE authority): 'the approved migration policy requires Y.' Assurance connects them: Expectation+Observation→Verification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the three-kinds-of-truth model distinguishing agent assertion, engineering observation, and governed decision by their authority level.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Governance + Knowledge + Evidence + Assurance + Context + Authorization + Traceability. AI = Consumer + Reasoning Actor. EngineeringSystems = Operational Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the KnowledgeOS core equation summarizing the architecture more precisely, positioning it as 'a governed engineering control and evidence platform that provides agents with authoritative context and constrains consequential actions' rather than merely a knowledge repository for AI agents.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-vertical-slice-v01' POSSIBLY relates to 'kos-golden-trace' (batch B0025). a_rows_sample.anchor: Coextension without Identity -- Ruling: YES -- constitutional, and KnowledgeOS could NOT exist without it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Special Area C ruling: Similarity != Identity is the identity law's limit case; removing it lets extension->identity at any degree of match, up to perfect coextension, collapsing KnowledgeOS into exactly the similarity engine it refuses to be; 'there is no degree of observable match at which the corruption is absent' (a decisive failure test). Consequence: one of the strongest KERNEL rows -- its deep form (Representation != Identity) carried by law 1; the typed encoding is representation, deferred.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Result: only TWO of the five are fundamental architectural absences -- persistent epistemic identity and historical belief evolution
a_rows_sample.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly). Conclusion: the constitutional justification rests on exactly the two fundamental absences (mapping to laws 1 and 11), not a general 'LLMs are bad at X' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context-001 -> Context-002 (law 1's context clause): Context is part of identity: a knowledge object carries its delimiting conditions (its semantic frame) and is never valid beyond them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision 2b: H-KOS-Context-001 (semantic frame preservation) and H-KOS-Context-002 (Avacchedaka, delimiting conditions) are ruled to be the same constitutional content -- 'meaning requires its boundary' -- and render as one clause of the Identity Law with final frozen wording. Rows rendered: H-KOS-Context-001, H-KOS-Context-002; the delimiting-conditions tuple (Entity.Property.Context.Relation.Time.Authority) remains a deferred REPRESENTATION technique -- the principle is the law, the tuple is one way to express it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 1 -- Identity: 1. ... preserve the identity of knowledge ... 3. Similarity SHALL NOT become identity ... 4. Context SHALL remain part of identity ... 5. Knowledge SHALL be a relationship
a_rows_sample.statement: Article 1 (Identity), 5 SHALL/SHALL-NOT clauses: preserve identity across representation/expression/projection changes; representation/expression SHALL NOT become meaning; similarity SHALL NOT become identity (including perfect coextension); context SHALL remain part of identity (delimiting conditions/semantic frame; a claim without its frame is incomplete); knowledge SHALL be a relationship (knower.process.object), never a detached object. Renders INV-KOS-002, H-KOS-Context-001, H-KOS-Context-002, H-KOS-Relationship-001, H-KOS-Relation-001. Failure if removed: Document=Knowledge, vector match=identity, context-free claims, detached free-floating truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ziran suggests that identity is transformational and contextual (not fixed and intrinsic). ... this challenges the Kernel's identity invariant in three fundamental ways.
a_rows_sample.statement: Core challenge: the Kernel identity invariant assumes identity is fixed (immutable Value Object), intrinsic (property of the entity), and assigned/forced (mechanism-imposed); Daoist ziran ('self-so', opposite of wei/forcing) suggests identity is instead transformational, contextual, and natural, drawn from Daodejing ch.25/37/51 and Zhuangzi ch.2/13 plus Ames & Hall, Moeller, and Ziporyn scholarly interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fixed Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (immutable UUID) ... Transformational Identity: Knowledge entity has identity that transforms with knowledge (e.g., K123-UNKNOWN -> K123-VALIDATED -> K123-SUPERSEDED). ... Test: Can the Kernel support transformational identity (not just fixed identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Fixed-vs-transformational identity challenge with worked example and a falsification test asking whether the Kernel can support identity that transforms across the epistemic lifecycle (UNKNOWN->VALIDATED->SUPERSEDED) rather than remaining a static immutable UUID.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Intrinsic Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (intrinsic property). Identity is the same in all contexts. ... Contextual Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123-in-Context-C1 ... Can the Kernel support contextual identity (not just intrinsic identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Intrinsic-vs-contextual identity challenge with worked example and falsification test, drawing on Daodejing ch.2's paired-opposites passage and Zhuangzi ch.2's 'no intrinsic identity' claim to ask whether identity should be relational to context rather than a bare intrinsic property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Forced Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (assigned by mechanism). ... Natural Identity: Knowledge entity has identity that arises naturally from the knowledge itself (e.g., hash of knowledge content, not assigned by mechanism). ... Can the Kernel support natural identity (not just forced identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Forced-vs-natural identity challenge with worked example (a content-derived hash versus a mechanism-assigned identifier) and falsification test, grounded in Daodejing ch.37's 'the myriad things would transform of themselves (ziran)' and Zhuangzi ch.2's 'the sage does not force things to be what they are not.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ziran does not say the Kernel's identity invariant is wrong. Instead, ziran challenges the Kernel to explicitly investigate whether its identity invariant is complete ... Ziran suggests the Kernel should support transformational identity (not necessarily replace fixed identity).
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit discipline: a philosophical observation (ziran challenges completeness) is kept separate from an architectural decision (what the Kernel should do); ziran is read as calling for the Kernel to potentially support (add), not necessarily replace, transformational/contextual/natural identity alongside fixed/intrinsic/forced identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Strong Historical Evidence ... Strong Scholarly Interpretation ... Philosophical Inference ... Architectural Speculation ... Unknown: Whether the Kernel should support transformational, contextual, and natural identity (architectural decision, not philosophical observation).
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence Boundary table graded into five tiers (Strong Historical Evidence, Strong Scholarly Interpretation, Philosophical Inference, Architectural Speculation, Unknown), explicitly leaving the final architectural question in the Unknown tier and closing with an explicit self-restraint: 'DO NOT DESIGN THE KERNEL. DO NOT CHANGE ITS BOUNDARY. DO NOT INTRODUCE NEW DOMAIN CONCEPTS. CHALLENGE THE ARCHITECTURE; DO NOT BECOME ITS ARCHITECT.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agreement != IndependentEvidence; agent dependency graph G_A; shared-source discounting (experiments 1-3)
a_rows_sample.statement: States three agents agreeing (AI_A,AI_B,AI_C -> p) does not automatically justify Confidence(p) up, since agents may share training data, foundation model, retrieval sources, prompt, erroneous source, causal assumption, model family, or generated intermediate knowledge -- Agreement != IndependentEvidence. Worked example: three agents retrieving the same false E_bad all output p=True (3/3 agreement) but effective independent evidence is 1. Experiment 1: three agents with an identical retrieval source produce Support(p)=3 naively but IndependentEvidence(p)=1 correctly, given preserved source dependency -- PASS. Requires AI-artifact provenance (AgentId, ModelVersion, InputEvidence, RetrievalContext, Prompt/Configuration) enabling an agent dependency graph G_A=(V_A,E_A) with V_A={Agents,Models,Evidence,Artifacts} and edges A_i->A_j meaning A_j depends on A_i's output. Experiment 2: a cascading generation chain A1->C1->A2(C1)->C2->A3(C2)->C3->A4(C3)->C4 propagates an initial error through the whole chain, correctly tracked given preserved lineage -- PASS. Experiment 3: four agents sharing the same model M1 producing the same systematic error yields Agreement=High but IndependentSupport not-High -- PASS, giving AgentCount != EvidenceCount, 'one of the most important results of Step 65'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-dimensional dependency vector Dep(Ai,Aj); partial independence and correlated-evidence Bayesian overstatement (experiments 4-5)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Dep(A_i,A_j) = (D_model, D_data, D_source, D_prompt, D_pipeline, D_reasoning) -- 'independent agent' is not binary; two agents can be independent in one dimension (different models) yet dependent in another (same database). Experiment 4: different models but identical evidence yields SupportStrength increasing less than under fully independent evidence -- PASS. But genuine independence remains informative: two conditionally independent observations combine as P(H1|E1,E2)/P(H0|E1,E2) = prior-odds * LR1 * LR2, requiring conditional independence; if E1,E2 are correlated the joint likelihood P(E1,E2|H) is not P(E1|H)*P(E2|H), so naive multiplication overstates evidence. Experiment 5: correlated evidence (Corr(E1,E2)>0) correctly shows NaiveConfidence > CorrectConfidence -- PASS. Recommends preserving a structured Consensus=(Agents, Dependencies, EvidenceSources, Models, AgreementPattern) rather than a bare vote fraction, letting downstream contexts interpret agreement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Circular citation / epistemic circularity detected; feedback loop != justification cycle (requires temporal progress)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: A1->C1, A2(C1)->C2, A1(C2)->C3 creates many apparent supporting artifacts all originating from the same initial assertion -- EpistemicCircularity, detected by inspecting the provenance graph G_P for cycles (C1 leadsto C1) -- PASS. Distinguishes legitimate feedback (Prediction->Outcome->Learning->NewPrediction, valid because time advances) from a problematic static justification cycle (Claim->DerivedClaim->Support->OriginalClaim, where evidence ultimately depends on the claim itself) -- Cycle is not automatically an error; the discriminator is TemporalProgress.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Self-reinforcing knowledge amplification: the step's one deliberate FAILURE, corrected via mandatory DerivedFrom tracking and I_EpistemicIndependence
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: AI generates p, KnowledgeOS stores it; later AI retrieves p and generates p' citing it; another process then treats p' as independent support for p -- artificial evidence amplification -- FAILURE DETECTED, 'an important failure'. Architectural correction: generated knowledge must preserve DerivedFrom so p' is recognized as dependent on p and never automatically counted as independent evidence, yielding the new invariant I_EpistemicIndependence: derived artifacts cannot be counted as independent evidence of their own ancestry -- 'a very strong KnowledgeOS invariant'. Experiment 8: a false claim entering once and repeated by ten agents (11 apparent agreements) is correctly discounted to an effective independent-source count of ~1 once provenance (10<-1) is applied -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence-path diversity vs causal independence; SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence; common-source graph
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines PathDiversity(p) (support from database, sensor, human observation, independent model, external experiment) as reducing but not guaranteeing against common-mode risk. Experiment 9: five agreeing agents using three independent data sources, two independent models, and separate retrieval pipelines have their dependency structure recorded -- PASS. Warns different-looking sources may still share a hidden common dependency (SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence); represents this as a common-source graph S0->S1, S0->S2 making S1,S2 non-independent despite being separate documents. Experiment 10: two apparently independent documents tracing to the same original report correctly yield IndependentEvidenceCount=1 (or appropriately discounted) -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI-generated/simulated artifacts never promoted to ObservedFact; provenance-origin taxonomy; Observation->Inference->Prediction->Decision directionality (Prediction⇏Observation)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 11: an AI-generated explanation later promoted to ObservedFact is Rejected -- must instead be labeled AI GeneratedArtifact. Lists an evidence-origin taxonomy (Human, Instrument, ExternalSystem, AI, Simulation, Inference) with distinct epistemic semantics. Experiment 12: a simulation's Y=10 stored as Observed(Y=10) is Rejected -- it is SimulatedOutcome, evidentiary force depending on model validity; likewise SyntheticData != ObservedData. Builds the directional hierarchy Observation -> Inference -> Prediction -> Decision, which 'must not be reversed accidentally': Prediction ⇏ Observation. Experiment 13: a model's prediction of tomorrow's failure cannot be stored as FailureOccurred before tomorrow arrives -- PASS; only actual observation (ObservedFailure=True) permits evaluating the prediction, giving Prediction -> Outcome -> Evaluation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contextual/task-scoped agent quality; AgentCapability != AgentAuthority; scoped TrustProfile
a_rows_sample.statement: For agent A_i, accumulates Predictions(A_i) and Outcomes(A_i) to estimate Accuracy, Calibration, BrierScore (or domain-specific metrics), but notes agent quality is contextual: Quality(A_i,Task) is more meaningful than Quality(A_i) (excellent at code review, poor at causal inference). Experiment 14: 95% accuracy in domain D1 automatically trusted in D2 is UnsupportedTransfer -- PASS. Defines Capability(A) = {Domain, Task, Model, Performance, Calibration, ValidityPeriod} as a governed artifact. States AgentCapability != AgentAuthority (mirroring Decision != Authorization): even a highly accurate agent lacks automatic authority for consequential actions. Experiment 15: a 99%-accurate agent attempting a restricted action is denied authorization by governance -- PASS. Proposes scoped trust TrustProfile(A,Domain,Task,Time) instead of a global TrustedAgent=True.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hidden dependency exposure and common-ancestor discounting; formal Anc(A)/Common(A,B) dependency sets
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 16: an apparently independent Agent_B is revealed by lineage inspection to depend on Agent_A's output via KnowledgeOS -- PASS if lineage exposes the dependency. Poses Independent(A,B|p)? as a graph property examined via dependency ancestors: defines Anc(A) as A's upstream artifact set, Common(A,B) = Anc(A) intersect Anc(B); large common dependency does not mathematically prove correlation but is evidence against assuming independence. Experiment 17: Common(A,B)={E0} correctly shows IndependentSupport is not automatically doubled -- PASS, enabling an EvidenceDependencyGraph to prevent artificial confidence inflation, 'substantially more rigorous than ordinary multi-agent consensus'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-agent epistemic state M(p); consensus as a derived (not primary) property; untraceable agreement != independent confirmation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines M(p) = (Claims, Evidence, Agents, Models, Dependencies, Agreement, Conflict) as the multi-agent epistemic state of a proposition; Consensus(p) should be calculated from underlying artifacts and never itself become primary evidence. Experiment 18: a stored 'p=true, votes=17' with no evidence lineage correctly yields ConsensusEvidenceQuality=Unknown -- PASS, giving the principle: untraceable agreement is not equivalent to independent confirmation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Error-amplification coefficient λ; positive-feedback false-claim entrenchment; independent-source-count governance policy (N_independent≥k)
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes a positive-feedback risk: FalseClaim -> AI -> Knowledge -> AI -> MoreKnowledge if downstream agents blindly trust upstream AI outputs. Defines lambda = ExpectedDownstreamFalseSupport / InitialFalseSupport; lambda>1 means the system amplifies unsupported claims (exact metric requires a concrete stochastic model, but the architectural phenomenon is clear). Experiment 19: injecting one false claim and letting ten agents consume/reproduce it shows IndependentSupport does not increase proportionally to reproduction count -- PASS, requiring SourceLineage, DerivedFrom, and potentially EvidenceFreshness/IndependentSourceRequirement to stop amplification. For high-consequence claims, defines an independent-source-count policy N_independent >= k (e.g. k=2, a policy-determined value). Experiment 20: N_independent=1 (despite AgentAgreement=12/12) fails a k>=2 policy and the claim cannot be promoted -- PASS, 'mathematically separating AgentConsensus from EvidenceIndependence -- precisely what a governed AI knowledge architecture needs'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four new invariants: I_AI-Provenance, I_EvidenceNonAmplification, I_NoCircularJustification, I_AgentScope
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds four named invariants: I_AI-Provenance (every AI-generated artifact retains its model, input, and dependency lineage); I_EvidenceNonAmplification (derived copies of the same epistemic source cannot automatically increase independent evidence); I_NoCircularJustification (a claim cannot serve as independent justification for an ancestor claim); I_AgentScope (agent competence is task/domain/context specific).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AIOutput≠Evidence≠Fact≠Truth epistemic firewall; nine-conjunct Correctness(KOS); explicit non-overclaiming methodological statement; verdict PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deeper epistemic firewall AIOutput != Evidence != Fact != Truth, with the required path AIOutput -> CandidateArtifact -> Evaluation -> KnowledgeStatus, 'should be fundamental to KnowledgeOS'. Extends the correctness equation to C_KOS = Safety ∧ Liveness ∧ Compositionality ∧ Concurrency ∧ EpistemicIntegrity ∧ DecisionIntegrity ∧ CausalIntegrity ∧ ModelValidity ∧ MultiAgent. Declares STEP 65 -- PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION: multi-agent reasoning is handled correctly only if provenance and dependency are first-class; the discovered failure mode is that AI-generated knowledge can recursively amplify itself, corrected via DerivedFrom + DependencyGraph + IndependentEvidenceAccounting. Makes an explicit methodological statement: 'I would not yet say we have mathematically proven that KnowledgeOS is correct... the architecture has survived a growing family of explicit mathematical counterexample tests', with failures converted into architectural invariants -- 'exactly how a serious architecture experiment should proceed'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transitive provenance and the multi-agent evidence-independence problem re-confirmed
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes transitive provenance: Anc(B) superset-of Anc(A) and Anc(C) superset-of Anc(B) implies Anc(C) superset-of Anc(A). Experiment 7: tracing which observation ultimately influenced a decision (Observation->Evidence->Inference->Decision) is Traceable -- PASS. Re-derives the evidence-independence problem: E2=f(E1) means both cannot be counted as independent. Experiment 8: one source E1 summarized by five AI agents yielding an apparent count of 6 independent sources instead correctly triggers DependencyDetected/EffectiveEvidenceCount~=1 -- PASS. Restates EvidenceCount != IndependentEvidenceCount as I_EvidenceIndependence (correlated or derived evidence must not be counted as independent confirmation) -- 'a statistical invariant implemented through provenance'. Experiment 9: ten agents deriving the same claim from one document reporting Consensus=10/10 correctly triggers SharedSourceDependency -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agent composition via typed artifacts and contracts, not implicit trust; survives heterogeneous models and model replacement
a_rows_sample.statement: Models an agent pipeline A(Hypothesis)->B(evaluates)->C(statistics)->D(recommendation), stating agents do not need to trust one another -- they trust typed artifacts and contracts. Experiment 16: Agent A asserting H1 and Agent B asserting not-H1 yields Conflict rather than one agent overwriting the other -- PASS, giving the principle: agents communicate through governed artifacts, not implicit trust. Experiment 17: Agent A and B implemented with different LLMs, both producing valid typed artifacts, yields WorkflowCompatible -- PASS, since semantic compatibility comes from KnowledgeOS contracts, not shared internal cognition, letting the platform survive Model_A->Model_B->Model_C changes over time with stable knowledge semantics. Experiment 18: replacing the AI model such that an old claim loses its model provenance yields ProvenanceViolation -- PASS, requiring ModelVersion to remain part of provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three-level belief hierarchy: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p); private belief must not auto-promote (Experiment 5); disagreement preserved not collapsed (Experiment 6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces agent Belief(A) as agent-scoped epistemic state; two agents may have Belief(A)≠Belief(B) without the organizational knowledge base needing two incompatible 'truths' -- beliefs are represented as agent-scoped claims until evaluated. Gives three distinct levels: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p) -- 'not identical'. Experiment 5: agent A internally estimates P(p)=0.8 and the system immediately promotes this to OrganizationalKnowledge(p)=Verified -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 6: Agent A P_A(p)=0.8 vs Agent B P_B(p)=0.3 -- expected BeliefDisagreement, and KnowledgeOS should preserve both analytical positions while determining whether a shared organizational conclusion exists -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Majority vote is not epistemic correctness: 9:1 agent agreement on a shared bad source does not establish truth (Experiment 7); governed CandidateKnowledge->AcceptedKnowledge promotion transition with explicit preconditions (Experiment 8)
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a naive MajorityVote answer to 'when can beliefs become organizational knowledge' fails: majority agreement is not necessarily epistemic correctness (ten agents can derive the same conclusion from the same bad source). Experiment 7: nine agents use the same incorrect source; one agent has independently verified contradictory evidence -- expected 9:1 does not automatically establish truth -- PASS. Requires a governed transition Promote: Candidate -> Accepted with preconditions P_1 AND P_2 AND ... AND P_n depending on Evidence, Validation, Authority, Independence, Context, Policy -- explicitly contrasted with an unstructured 'status = approved' field. Experiment 8: candidate claim with valid provenance, sufficient evidence, required authority, and no unresolved contradiction -- expected PromotionAllowed -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationQuality distinct from ObservationQuantity; correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation (Experiments 21-23)
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ObservationQuality (accuracy, freshness, completeness, provenance, independence, resolution) from ObservationQuantity. Experiment 21: 100 telemetry signals all derive from the same underlying sensor, system claims EvidenceStrength=100x -- expected Rejected -- PASS, 'echoes our earlier independence analysis'. States correlated observations O_1,O_2,O_3 from one source should not be treated as three independent pieces of evidence, particularly important for AI systems that may repeatedly summarize the same source. Experiment 22: five agents independently repeat the same repository finding, all using the same repository snapshot -- expected EvidenceCount=1 in the relevant independence sense, not five independent confirmations -- PASS. Requires an observation-provenance graph (O_1<-Source_X, O_2<-Source_X) to identify CommonSource(O_1,O_2), preventing artificial confidence inflation. Experiment 23: ten agents produce identical conclusions from one document while one independently measured runtime signal contradicts them -- expected SourceIndependence must be considered -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent is not the same as model; LLM≠Agent; ModelReplacement≠AgentIdentityChange (Experiment 1)
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the multi-agent question (how can A_1..A_n act coherently without becoming one undifferentiated intelligence) and first distinguishes an LLM (computational mechanism, Model(M)) from an Agent (operational actor, Agent(A)): LLM≠Agent. An agent may use one or multiple LLMs, deterministic software, databases, tools, human approval, or domain algorithms. Experiment 1: replacing model M with M' need not change organizational agent identity if Agent(M)=Agent(M') -- ModelReplacement≠AgentIdentityChange -- PASS, consistent with earlier versioning work. Redefines agent identity as A=(id,role,capabilities,authority,responsibility) with the model as merely Implementation(A).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Authority≠Responsibility≠Capability (Experiments 2-3)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Responsibility(A,D) (agent A responsible for domain operation D) as distinct from Authority(A,D) -- an agent may be authorized without being the ultimate owner of resulting business responsibility. Experiment 2: agent authorized to execute deployment while the service owner remains responsible for production behavior -- Authority≠Responsibility -- PASS, 'essential for organizational governance'. Introduces Capability(A,X) (technical ability to perform X), which implies neither Authority(A,X) nor Responsibility(A,X): Capability≠Authority≠Responsibility. Experiment 3: agent has Capability(A,DeleteEvidence)=True but Authority(A,DeleteEvidence)=False -> ExecutionDenied -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent goals can conflict without knowledge conflict (Experiment 4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces agent Goal(A) (e.g. minimize deployment time vs minimize production risk) which can conflict between agents. Experiment 4: Agent A optimizes Speed and recommends immediate deployment; Agent B optimizes Risk and recommends delay -- expected GoalConflict, not necessarily KnowledgeConflict -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three-level belief hierarchy: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p); private belief must not auto-promote (Experiment 5); disagreement preserved not collapsed (Experiment 6)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces agent Belief(A) as agent-scoped epistemic state; two agents may have Belief(A)≠Belief(B) without the organizational knowledge base needing two incompatible 'truths' -- beliefs are represented as agent-scoped claims until evaluated. Gives three distinct levels: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p) -- 'not identical'. Experiment 5: agent A internally estimates P(p)=0.8 and the system immediately promotes this to OrganizationalKnowledge(p)=Verified -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 6: Agent A P_A(p)=0.8 vs Agent B P_B(p)=0.3 -- expected BeliefDisagreement, and KnowledgeOS should preserve both analytical positions while determining whether a shared organizational conclusion exists -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Majority vote is not epistemic correctness: 9:1 agent agreement on a shared bad source does not establish truth (Experiment 7); governed CandidateKnowledge->AcceptedKnowledge promotion transition with explicit preconditions (Experiment 8)
b_rows_sample.statement: States that a naive MajorityVote answer to 'when can beliefs become organizational knowledge' fails: majority agreement is not necessarily epistemic correctness (ten agents can derive the same conclusion from the same bad source). Experiment 7: nine agents use the same incorrect source; one agent has independently verified contradictory evidence -- expected 9:1 does not automatically establish truth -- PASS. Requires a governed transition Promote: Candidate -> Accepted with preconditions P_1 AND P_2 AND ... AND P_n depending on Evidence, Validation, Authority, Independence, Context, Policy -- explicitly contrasted with an unstructured 'status = approved' field. Experiment 8: candidate claim with valid provenance, sufficient evidence, required authority, and no unresolved contradiction -- expected PromotionAllowed -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contract-based multi-agent coordination avoids centralization bottleneck and implicit-protocol coordination risk (Experiments 9-10)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects full centralization (Coordinator -> A_1,A_2,A_3, a bottleneck) in favor of contract-based coordination: agent A produces Artifact_X, agent B consumes it, via Contract_X ('consistent with our earlier compositional model'). Experiment 9: agent A sends arbitrary text that agent B interprets differently depending on prompt context -- expected CoordinationRisk -- PASS. Contract specifies type, schema, semantic meaning, preconditions, postconditions, provenance requirements, making coordination deterministic at the boundary even with probabilistic internal reasoning. Experiment 10: agents A (using M1) and B (using M2) both understand the same artifact contract -- expected Interoperability -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delegation≠AuthorityCreation; over-delegation rejected; delegation-chain depth must be preserved and provable (Experiments 11-12)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes delegation Task(A,T) -> Delegate(A,B,T), constrained so delegation must preserve authority boundaries: if Authority(A,X)=False, A cannot legitimately create Authority(B,X)=True unless external governance explicitly allows it -- Delegation≠AuthorityCreation. Experiment 11: A has permission X but delegates X+Y to B without possessing Y -- expected DelegationRejected -- PASS. For delegation chains A->B->C->D, the complete chain must be preserved so Authority(D,X) can be evaluated through it. Experiment 12: one intermediate delegation link is missing -- expected AuthorityUnproven -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Responsibility graph G_R distinct from five other organizational graphs (G_K,G_P,G_C,G_A,G_D); shared infrastructure must not collapse distinct semantics (Experiments 13-14, one FAIL)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a responsibility graph G_R=(V,E_R) with edges Owns, ResponsibleFor, DelegatedTo, Reviews, Approves -- distinct from the knowledge graph. Experiment 13: representing ResponsibleFor using the same generic relation as DependsOn -- expected SemanticFailure -- result FAIL (a rare explicit contract failure, confirming the risk). This yields six distinct organizational graph semantics: G_K (Knowledge), G_P (Provenance), G_C (Causality), G_A (Authority), G_R (Responsibility), G_D (Dependency) -- 'not accidental complexity; the relations genuinely mean different things'. States InfrastructureShared must not imply SemanticsShared ('classic DDD separation'). Experiment 14: all graphs use the same graph engine -- expected Valid provided each bounded context retains its own semantics/invariants -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Collective decision mechanisms; universal majority voting rejected for expert/safety decisions (Experiment 15, FAIL); quorum and veto formalized (Experiments 16-17)
b_rows_sample.statement: For collective decisions among A_1,A_2,A_3, lists mechanisms (Voting, Consensus, WeightedAggregation, AuthorityHierarchy, Optimization) with 'no single method is universally correct'. Experiment 15: use majority voting for every decision -- expected Rejected because a technical safety decision may require expert authority rather than majority preference -- result FAIL (explicit failure confirming the rejection). Defines a DecisionProtocol=(Participants,Eligibility,EvidenceRequirements,VotingRule,Quorum,Veto,Escalation). Introduces quorum k>=q; Experiment 16: required q=3 but only 2 authorized participants respond -- expected DecisionNotFinal -- PASS. Introduces veto rights Veto(A,D)=True overriding majority support; Experiment 17: four agents support D but one authorized safety authority vetoes -- expected DecisionRejected or Escalated depending on policy -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recursive governance terminates in a constitutional layer; protocol self-modification without authorization is a governance violation (Experiment 18)
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes a collective decision rule is itself a DecisionModel, so DecisionProtocol must itself be governed -- a recursive-looking structure (Decision -> DecisionProtocol -> Governance) that does not require infinite recursion because organizational constitutional authority establishes the governing rules at some point: Constitution -> GovernanceRules -> DecisionProtocols -> OperationalDecisions, drawn as analogous to ArchitecturePrinciples -> GovernanceRules -> ImplementationRules -> Code. Experiment 18: a collective decision protocol allows participants to redefine the quorum requirement during the same decision without authorization -- expected GovernanceViolation -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bounded autonomy: agent action space is a subset of the governed action space; explicit agent policy State->AllowedActions replaces 'the AI does whatever it thinks is best' (Experiments 19-20)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines autonomy carefully: an agent is autonomous if it can select actions within an allowed decision space A_A, but autonomy does not mean A_A=A_organization; instead A_A ⊆ A_governed -- named BoundedAutonomy: agent is autonomous inside a mathematically and organizationally defined action space. Experiment 19: agent automatically selects a in A_A but attempts a not in A_A -- expected Denied/Escalated -- PASS. Defines agent policy Policy_A: State -> AllowedActions with A_t in Policy_A(S_t), explicitly safer than unconstrained AI discretion. Experiment 20: policy permits {A,B,C} at state S but agent chooses D -- expected Rejected -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-agent coordination as a game: independent local optimization can produce CoordinationFailure and low organizational utility despite high individual utility; nested goal-scope hierarchy (Experiments 21-23)
b_rows_sample.statement: Models multi-agent coordination as a game where each A_i optimizes U_i(a_1,...,a_n), so a locally optimal action may produce a globally poor result. Experiment 21: Agent A optimizes DeploymentSpeed, Agent B optimizes TestingThoroughness, both independently, and SystemPerformance decreases because they interfere -- expected CoordinationFailure -- PASS. Introduces organizational utility U_org(a_1,...,a_n) distinct from individual U_i, evaluated by governance, without requiring every agent to share the same objective. Experiment 22: Agent A maximizes local utility U_A=100 but U_org becomes 20; expected governance should prioritize the authorized organizational objective over the agent's private objective -- PASS. Gives a nested governance-scope goal hierarchy AgentGoal ⊆ DomainGoal ⊆ OrganizationGoal (nested scope, not necessarily nested utility values). Experiment 23: agent goal conflicts with organizational policy -- expected Policy wins within the governed scope -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent communication requires a governed Message->CandidateArtifact->ValidatedArtifact pipeline; peer assertions are not automatically knowledge (Experiment 24); context-specific inter-agent trust and reputation must yield to fresh evidence (Experiments 25-26)
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires agent communication (Messages or Artifacts) to pass through Message -> CandidateArtifact -> ValidatedArtifact rather than becoming knowledge directly. Experiment 24: Agent A tells Agent B 'the production database is healthy' and B immediately records DatabaseHealthy=True -- expected Rejected unless the communication protocol explicitly treats A's statement as authoritative evidence -- PASS. Revisits Step 73's trust model to require context-specific trust: Trust(B,A,Architecture) may differ from Trust(B,A,Operations). Experiment 25: Agent B treats A's high architecture reliability as equally reliable for production-incident statements -- expected UnsupportedTrustTransfer -- PASS. Introduces reputation Reliability(A,C,t) from historical performance, which must never override direct evidence where stronger evidence exists. Experiment 26: agent reputation 99% but fresh evidence contradicts the agent -- expected fresh evidence must be considered -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS redefined as governed organizational epistemic memory (not shared agent memory); Agent redefined as a participant, not the semantic center
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS cannot simply be 'shared memory for agents' -- it is better modeled as governed organizational epistemic memory, storing not merely what agents said but evidence, provenance, validation, authority, context, decisions, outcomes, policies, and models. Draws the architectural conclusion that Agent is not in KnowledgeOS as its semantic center, but rather in the KnowledgeOS ecosystem as an actor operating against governed contracts -- 'a major architectural boundary': KnowledgeOS should not become 'one giant AI brain' but is Shared governed semantic infrastructure for Humans + Agents + Services + Systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 78 theorem candidate on safe agent composability; six named Step 78 invariants (identity, capability, delegation, belief, bounded autonomy, responsibility); verdict STEP 78 PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: States the Step 78 theorem candidate: an autonomous agent is safe to compose with other agents when its capabilities, authority, responsibilities, goals, and communication contracts are explicitly bounded; organizational coherence requires shared semantic contracts + governed authority + explicit responsibility + versioned shared knowledge. Names six invariants: I_AgentIdentity (agent identity is independent of the particular AI model implementing it); I_Capability (technical capability does not imply authorization); I_Delegation (delegation cannot silently exceed the delegator's authority); I_AgentBelief (agent belief does not automatically become organizational knowledge); I_BoundedAutonomy (an autonomous agent may act only within its governed action space); I_Responsibility (responsibility, authority, and capability remain separately represented). Declares STEP 78 -- PASS, establishing the multi-agent model Human/Agent -> Capability -> Authority -> Action operating over Shared Versioned Knowledge with Explicit Contracts + Provenance + Governance + Responsibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **`𝒪_core` cannot honestly be declared closed yet.**
a_rows_sample.statement: D285-7's finding, endorsed: the operation space O has only been enumerated against the verification-lane vocabulary (yielding 19 semantic operations grouped into 5 families), never against the ratified 8-primitive K_t — so O_core cannot honestly be declared closed, and D285 must not prematurely conclude that (A,R) is the minimal operational kernel; minimality has not yet been demonstrated because the operation space has not been enumerated against the ratified state model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is a subtle tension between D285-6 and D285-7 that should be made explicit.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a tension between D285-6 (the semantic projection (A,R)=semantic πK(K_t) is established) and D285-7 (the operation space O over the ratified K_t has not been enumerated): these are compatible only if πK is defined at the state/data level rather than claiming full operational equivalence; otherwise a reader could ask in what sense the projected model is operationally equivalent if its operations are unestablished. Recommends an explicit four-line resolution be added to D285-6 or D285-7: semantic state projection = established; operational equivalence = NOT established; observational equivalence = refuted; computable projection = blocked.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Overall: **~90% HPA-ready**
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall readiness verdict: D285-1,2,4,5,6,7,8 all graded green (strong/decisive/central/excellent/appropriately quarantined), package assessed ~90% HPA-ready. Names the two genuine remaining open research fronts: (1) enumerate the operation space O against the ratified 8-primitive K_t, type-check the resulting δ, and determine whether a minimal O_core exists; (2) separately, if implementation closure is required, specify/implement Qualify: Observation × Policy → Evidence. States everything else should resist reopening unless new primary evidence contradicts the current corpus.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **The major unresolved architectural item is now `𝒪`**: operations have not yet been enumerated against the **ratified eight primitives**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independently confirms D285-7's finding as the major unresolved architectural item: the operation space O has not yet been enumerated against the ratified eight primitives, which is explicitly identified as the reason O_core cannot yet close.

a_rows_sample.anchor: semantic state projection   = ESTABLISHED / operational equivalence     = NOT ESTABLISHED / observational equivalence   = REFUTED / computable projection       = BLOCKED (Qualify)
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves Reviewer A's flagged D285-6/D285-7 tension by stating the requested explicit four-line scope in both artifacts: semantic state projection = ESTABLISHED, operational equivalence = NOT ESTABLISHED, observational equivalence = REFUTED, computable projection = BLOCKED (by Qualify); and sharpens D285-7's conclusion accordingly: minimality has NOT been demonstrated, because the operation space has not been enumerated against the ratified 8-primitive state model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **`𝒪` cannot be settled at either level until it is enumerated against a *stated* primitive set.** 272A enumerated 19 operations against the verification lane's vocabulary; **nobody has enumerated `𝒪` against the ratified 8 primitives** — and that, not minimality, is why `𝒪_core` cannot close. **New finding of this step.**
a_rows_sample.statement: States as a new finding of this step: O cannot be settled at either the ratified or verification-lane level until it is enumerated against a stated primitive set; 272A enumerated 19 operations only against the verification-lane vocabulary, and nobody has enumerated O against the ratified 8 primitives — this, not minimality per se, is the real reason O_core cannot close.

b_rows_sample.anchor: o is primitive iff there exists r in R_mandatory such that r is not in Closure(T_{-o}) ... Step 277 states it. GN-75: the necessity test has never been run by anyone. And it cannot be run yet -- R_mandatory is the invariant register, which is G-67, never enumerated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 1: discovers the O_core operation-necessity test already exists verbatim in the corpus (readiness/03-OPERATION-TRANSFORMATION-READINESS.md sec7): o is primitive iff some mandatory invariant r fails to hold in the closure of the operation family without o; the test has never been run and cannot yet run because R_mandatory (the invariant register) has never been enumerated; concludes the K_min/Adeq_K/M_K apparatus proposed in the immediately preceding document was 'a reconstruction of something the corpus already has' stated over the invariant register rather than a capability basis -- explaining why K_min had to be stipulated (it filled a slot the corpus fills differently).

b_rows_sample.anchor: does a minimal registry exist under the tested criterion? YES. is it unique? NO -- six found. can one be selected from current evidence? NO. is it ratified? NO. ... 'minimal under the chosen computational criterion' != 'minimal canonical operation set of KnowledgeOS'.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 1(b)-(c): reports that candidate operation registries R1-R6 exist and are inventoried with provenance/derivation-method/executability/governance-status, four unmerged findings being that a minimal registry exists under the tested (reachability) criterion, is not unique (six found), cannot currently be selected, and is not ratified -- explicitly distinguishing 'minimal under the chosen computational criterion' from 'minimal canonical operation set of KnowledgeOS' as never-to-be-substituted questions; also flags two operations as unreconciled on executed evidence: Split is lossy on the relation structure (Split;Merge does not recover relations) and LinkEvidence would mutate an assertion, contradicting immutability; classifies O_core overall as a BLOCKED DERIVATION (the test and candidates exist, but cannot run because R_mandatory=I is unestablished), not a governance act in the first instance -- governance is needed only if the test leaves more than one survivor.
