Undefined symbols: I(.) (deferred), S_B (depends on undefined 'legitimate'), T_1, A_I/G_I/D_I, Preserve(.), RequiredProvenance(R_C), Knowledge(E).

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 208
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Booleanization as a named anti-pattern; Suff(C,B,Task) (purpose-relative sufficiency); the four-layer split; Evidence != Claim; probability-of-proposition != truth-value-of-proposition; the explicit refusal to claim contracts are sufficient statistics; non-monotonicity as a requirement; the boxed claim 'the objective is not zero information loss, the objective is zero loss of relevant meaning' (the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement). Does not survive: L(C) as any quantity; I(A)<I(E) as a comparison; P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the Section 208.37 'provisional architectural theorem' (Sufficiency+Provenance+Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety), which is a definition dressed as an implication since Contract Safety is not independently defined -- not a theorem in any sense, a naming convention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
a_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 208 load-bearing boxed claims: Semantic Sufficiency, the provisional Contract-Safety theorem, and the survivor 'zero loss of relevant meaning'
a_rows_sample.statement: Three load-bearing boxed claims of Step 208, adjudicated: (1) 'Semantic Sufficiency: S_B⊆I(C(A))' -- the file's central definition, resting on the undefined I(.) and the undefined 'legitimate responsibility' in S_B. (2) 'Semantic Sufficiency + Provenance Preservation + Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety' -- self-labelled 'a provisional architectural theorem, not a mathematically proven theorem'; verifier judges it a stipulative definition of Contract Safety rather than an implication, since the consequent is not independently defined. (3) 'The objective is not zero information loss. The objective is zero loss of relevant meaning.' -- survives; the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F | D | P | U ... F = Fact ... D = Derived ... P = Proposed ... U = Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way epistemic classification for every architectural statement: F=Fact (directly supported by engineering evidence), D=Derived (logically derived from facts/observations), P=Proposed (a recommendation or future design), U=Unknown (insufficient evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We designed the system according to this architecture from the beginning ... That would be misleading. The intellectually stronger story is: Experience -> Problem -> Observation -> Experiment -> Pattern -> Abstraction -> Theory -> Architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against retrospectively rewriting the book's history as if the system had been designed according to the derived architecture from the beginning, calling this misleading; proposes instead the causal chain Experience->Problem->Observation->Experiment->Pattern->Abstraction->Theory->Architecture as the intellectually stronger and more honest narrative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How can this artifact support our current theory? We should ask: What does this artifact actually establish?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the archaeological method's central mindset shift: treat prior artifacts (prompts, AI outputs, architecture docs, ADRs, code, tests, rejected ideas, contradictions, revisions) as evidence to be asked 'what does this actually establish', never 'how does this support our current theory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E(A_j)={Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions} ... Artifact -> Evidence -> Interpretation. Not: Theory -> selective evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines evidence extraction per artifact E(A_j) as the set {Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions}, to be connected to architectural concepts only afterward (Artifact->Evidence->Interpretation), explicitly rejecting the reverse flow Theory->selective evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance enforcement could not yet be established from the available evidence ... unless we have evidence of absence
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that absence of knowledge about whether a property (e.g. provenance) exists in an implementation be written as Unknown ('could not yet be established from the available evidence'), never as an assertion of absence ('is missing') unless positive evidence of absence exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prov(C)={A_1,A_2,...,A_n} ... provenance of architecture itself
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes giving architectural claims themselves a provenance set Prov(C)={A_1,...,A_n} of supporting artifacts, so a reader can trace Claim->Evidence -- termed 'provenance of architecture itself'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ADL = Decision -> Problem -> Evidence -> Alternatives -> Rationale -> Consequence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Architecture Decision Lineage ADL = Decision->Problem->Evidence->Alternatives->Rationale->Consequence, proposed to eventually become part of the KnowledgeOS architecture itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Failure -> Knowledge ... some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches ... What did not work ... alongside ... What eventually worked. Otherwise the final architecture looks inevitable
b_rows_sample.statement: States the negative-result principle: a failed experiment (Hypothesis H tested, Result=not-H) is Failure->Knowledge, not useless, and some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches; the book should explicitly record what did not work alongside what eventually worked, because otherwise the final architecture looks falsely inevitable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ChosenPattern ... RejectedPattern ... ReasonForRejection
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects the negative-result principle to the corpus's Chapter 4 theme: knowledge includes discrimination between Valid and Invalid, so the architecture should preserve not only the ChosenPattern but sometimes the RejectedPattern and ReasonForRejection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_{t+1}=E(A_t, Evidence_t) ... Architecture is not merely documentation growth. It is knowledge evolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Models architecture evolution as A_{t+1}=E(A_t,Evidence_t) driven by new evidence, explicitly rejecting the weaker model A_{t+1}=A_t+more documentation; calls architecture 'knowledge evolution', not documentation growth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ΔA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an architecture-evolution tuple DeltaA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact) as the architecture's evolutionary provenance record for each change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stage 1 ... What problem was first recognized? ... Stage 7 What remains unverified?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing an 'epistemic chronology' (not necessarily calendar chronology) in seven stages: problem recognized, assumptions made, experiments challenging them, patterns emerged, abstractions introduced, resulting architecture, and what remains unverified -- proposed as the backbone of the eventual book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed Reality ... Architectural Interpretation ... Normative Design
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates three reconstruction layers: Observed Reality (what happened), Architectural Interpretation (what it means), and Normative Design (what should be built), illustrated with an AI-code-inconsistency example running observation->derived-knowledge->proposal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O=observations ... D=g(O)=derived knowledge ... P=h(D)=proposed architecture ... P ⇏ O
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes O->D->P (observations, derived knowledge via D=g(O), proposed architecture via P=h(D)) with the explicit non-implication P does-not-imply O: a proposal cannot retroactively become evidence for the observation that motivated it, protecting the book from circular reasoning (e.g. avoiding 'we need deterministic assurance because KnowledgeOS is a deterministic assurance platform').

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_fact=High if directly supported by primary implementation evidence ... C_derived=Medium if the inference depends on assumptions ... avoid false numerical precision
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a qualitative confidence label (e.g. C_fact=High, C_derived=Medium) attached to F/D/P/U claims only when justified, again warning against false numerical precision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Primary ... source code; configuration; database schema; test result; runtime behavior; direct experiment ... Secondary ... AI analysis; architecture summary; meeting notes; retrospective explanation. Secondary evidence ... should not silently override primary evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Primary evidence (source code, configuration, database schema, test result, runtime behavior, direct experiment) from Secondary evidence (AI analysis, architecture summary, meeting notes, retrospective explanation), warning that secondary evidence must not silently override primary evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AIClaim -> Hypothesis. Then: ImplementationEvidence -> Fact ... AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States that an AI-generated statement (e.g. Claude or DeepSeek claiming 'the system uses invariant-driven architecture') is not itself proof but a hypothesis, only becoming Fact once corroborated by implementation evidence; boxes the AI epistemic boundary AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence as one of the book's strongest intended methodological principles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We are using AI to reconstruct an architecture for an AI engineering platform ... The architecture is therefore being used to validate the method by which it is being reconstructed ... The method is correct because it follows the architecture [is circular]
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes the self-referential situation of using AI to reconstruct the architecture of an AI engineering platform (a useful meta-level experiment), then explicitly warns against circular validation ('the method is correct because it follows the architecture'); the reconstruction method must independently satisfy Evidence+Reproducibility+Traceability before it can be said to exemplify the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) ... Invariant -> Test -> Evidence. This creates a closed assurance loop
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Architecture Assurance Graph into an Evidence-Architecture-Graph EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) with edges Evidence->Claim->Decision->Architecture->Invariant and potentially Invariant->Test->Evidence, closing the assurance loop, then generalizes to the full cycle Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge, calling architecture 'a learning system'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Learning -> ArchitectureDrift ... Architecture evolution must itself be governed
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that ungoverned architectural learning becomes ArchitectureDrift, boxing the principle that architecture evolution must itself be governed, and lists six questions a software change should answer (what changed, why, which invariant is affected, which bounded context owns it, what evidence justifies it, how was it verified) as a stronger Software Change Governance model.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 277 -- Canonical Transformation Inventory and O_core Closure ... we cannot responsibly declare K minimal until we know what operations the state must support.
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 redirects the next step away from Part 1's recommendation (Policy/Authority interface formalization) to 'Step 277 -- Canonical Transformation Inventory and O_core Closure', on the ground that K-minimality cannot responsibly be declared before the complete transformation family T is established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State Transformation != Query != Governance Predicate != Representation Operation. This distinction is fundamental. ... Assert can change knowledge state. Whereas Query observes knowledge state. And Authorize determines whether an action is permitted.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the fundamental distinction driving Step 277's whole reduction: state transformation, query/observation, governance predicate and representation operation are four different mathematical roles that cannot be forced into one homogeneous operation algebra.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O = O_T ∪ O_E ∪ O_Q ∪ O_G ∪ O_R ... O_semantic != O_operational ... O_semantic != O_implementation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the corrected layered operation universe O = O_T (state transformations) ∪ O_E (evidence) ∪ O_Q (query/observation) ∪ O_G (governance) ∪ O_R (representation), replacing the previous flat O_core=O_S∪O_E∪O_H∪O_G∪O_Q∪O_X union, and states O_semantic != O_operational != O_implementation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_K = {t | t: K x I -> K'} ... A transformation may be partial: t: K x I ⇀ K ... Pre_t -> t -> K' -> Post_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the canonical partial state-transition schema t:K x I_t ⇀ K with explicit Pre_t/Post_t, arguing partiality is necessary because operations like Retract(K,p) with p not-in K or Supersede requiring evidence/temporal/authorization conditions cannot be pretended total.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assert, Retract, Supersede, Merge, Split ... We now test whether all five are genuinely primitive. ... Model A -- destructive removal ... Model B -- epistemic transition ... Because KnowledgeOS explicitly values history, provenance and replay, Model B is generally more compatible
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests each of the five historically-supported state operations for primitivity: Assert is REQUIRED; Retract's semantics remain an open choice between destructive removal (Model A) and a history-preserving epistemic-status transition (Model B), with Model B favoured as more compatible with KnowledgeOS's stated values; Supersede is REQUIRED and history-preserving by construction; Merge and Split are both flagged as only CANDIDATE primitives (possibly decomposable into Assert + conflict-resolution + linking, or into assertion-partitioning + relation-removal + lineage-preservation respectively), minimality unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay(K0,H) = fold(T,K0,H) ... If demonstrated, Replay need not be included in the primitive operation kernel. ... Trace, Query, Explain ... do not necessarily alter K. Therefore ... not in T_K.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues Replay is potentially a derived fold over the transformation sequence (Replay(K0,H)=fold(T,K0,H)) rather than a primitive operation, and that Trace/Query/Explain are observational (do not alter K) and so belong to the query layer O_Q, not the state-transition kernel T_K -- significantly shrinking the candidate primitive set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_candidate = {Assert, Retract, Supersede, Merge, Split, LinkEvidence} ... smaller != proven minimal. ... o is primitive iff exists r in R_mandatory : r not-in Closure(T_{-o})
a_rows_sample.statement: States the resulting candidate primitive kernel T_candidate={Assert,Retract,Supersede,Merge,Split,LinkEvidence} (reduced from ~20 heterogeneous operations), formalizes the operation-minimality criterion (o is primitive iff some mandatory distinction is lost by T minus {o}), and explicitly labels T_candidate as NOT YET PROVEN minimal -- the deletion/composability experiments remain future work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy does NOT disappear. ... we have separated semantic transition from authorization of transition. ... Policy gates transformations without necessarily becoming part of the knowledge-state representation itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that removing Authorize/Approve/Reject/ChangePolicy from the state-transition kernel does not solve Policy; it separates semantic transition from authorization-of-transition, with Policy acting as an external gate (Authorize(...) -> Decision -> transformation) rather than a stored component of K -- explicitly said to resolve part of the earlier circularity concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test T1 -- Assert elimination ... Test T4 -- Merge elimination ... Test T7 -- Replay derivation ... Test T8 -- Policy independence ... Test T9 -- Representation independence
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies nine mandatory falsification tests (T1-T9) for the next step: elimination tests for Assert/Retract/Supersede/Merge/Split/LinkEvidence (can each be expressed without the named primitive?), a derivation test for Replay-as-fold, a Policy-independence test (can t(K,i) be defined independently of Authorize?), and a representation-independence test (can two different serializations of the same semantic K be observationally equivalent?).

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **`𝒪_core`** | missing | §256.2 nine + §259.7 six; **14-element lower bound forced**, upper bound 18; Step 277 *"Classification: CLOSED"* | **RETIRED as "missing"** — open only on 4 operations' *mandatory* status (D-1) | ... | **Only one row still reads "unresolved with no owner": K-sufficiency.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Completes the mandate's required gap-status table across seven candidate gaps (O_core, Authority, Determination, K, Sigma, Transformation, K-sufficiency), finding six retired/derived/substantially-derived and only K-sufficiency left 'unresolved with no owner' — declared OPEN by Step 277 which explicitly commissioned a next step to test it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### PA-1 (`EXECUTED`, CRITICAL) — the commissioned K-sufficiency step was silently replaced ... Step 277 ends: "Next: STEP 278 — K-SUFFICIENCY AND TRANSFORMATION MINIMALITY TEST" The actual Step 278 is "POLICY–AUTHORITY INTEGRATION..." and it mentions K-sufficiency zero times.
a_rows_sample.statement: PA-1 (EXECUTED, CRITICAL): Step 277 explicitly commissions 'STEP 278 — K-SUFFICIENCY AND TRANSFORMATION MINIMALITY TEST' as its next step, but the actual Step 278 that was written is 'POLICY-AUTHORITY INTEGRATION, TEMPORAL SEMANTICS, AND GOVERNANCE CLOSURE', mentioning K-sufficiency zero times; its header claims to supersede an earlier draft of itself, not the commissioned step, and no artifact records the substitution. Identified as the fourth instance of the same corpus-wide 'commissioned-but-not-performed' failure mode (alongside the repaired measure-theory model, Regime, and Determination).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### PA-2 (`EXECUTED`, HIGH) — the estate adopted this session's numbers and dropped its method ... | congruence-vacuity (SO-2) | **0** | **NOT ADOPTED** |
a_rows_sample.statement: PA-2 (EXECUTED, HIGH): canonical-construction's BLOCKED-MANIFEST cites second-order's so_exp06_closure.py and reproduces its five closure percentages verbatim (so the package was read), yet a grep of Steps 272-278 shows the underlying methodological findings were NOT adopted: congruence-vacuity (0 occurrences), AuthorityAct typing (0), Context typing (0), R restored to 8 fields (0); invariant-expressibility mentioned only once. Step 277 declares K-sufficiency OPEN while its defining criterion (congruence plus invariant-expressibility) sits unadopted nearby — 'the estate took the measurements and left the instrument.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: 14-element lower bound forced by the corpus's own non-collapse laws; upper bound 18. Open only: are `Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce` mandatory? ... note independently: Qualify, Determine and Derive are forced by laws the corpus repeats 20, 19 and 18 times, yet appear in neither §256.2 nor §259.7.
a_rows_sample.statement: D-1 narrowed to whether four operations (Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce) are mandatory; K's ontology is invariant across all 16 possible resolutions, but the congruence proof and Minimality(K|T) are not (Step 277: 'Minimality: OPEN'). Independently notes that Qualify, Determine, and Derive are forced by corpus laws repeated 20/19/18 times respectively yet are absent from the two canonical operation-registry sections (§256.2, §259.7) — a gap regardless of which D-1 option is chosen.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## The one thing no decision covers ... K-sufficiency. Step 277 declares it OPEN and commissioned Step 278 to test it; Step 278 did Policy–Authority instead and mentions it zero times (PA-1). ... This needs no decision. It needs the commissioned step to actually be performed, with the criterion `Sufficient(K, 𝒪, ℐ)` rather than congruence alone.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes K-sufficiency from the six named decisions: unlike D-0 through D-5, K-sufficiency is not blocked by a normative choice but by a commissioned step (Step 278's original mandate) never having been performed. Recommends actually performing the K-sufficiency test using the Sufficient(K,O,I) criterion (congruence plus invariant-expressibility) rather than congruence alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⚠️ **G-16 moved to NARROWED — see [`05-ADDENDUM-STEP-272A.md`](./05-ADDENDUM-STEP-272A.md) §3.** Step 272A retracts Step 277's closure claim. **FULFILLED 9 → 8 · NARROWED 8 → 9.** Theoretical holes remain **11**.
a_rows_sample.statement: A retroactive correction note records that Step 272A (landing after this document's initial version) retracts Step 277's prior 'Classification: CLOSED' claim for O_core's transition-signature question (G-16), moving it from FULFILLED to NARROWED and revising the overall counts (FULFILLED 9->8, NARROWED 8->9, theoretical holes remaining at 11).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K-sufficiency (commissioned by 277 for 278)      occurrences=1    ADOPTED
a_rows_sample.statement: This later re-run reports K-sufficiency (the concept Step 277 commissioned Step 278 to test) as occurrences=1, ADOPTED -- directly contradicting the earlier finding in 01-STEP-272-PREMISE-AUDIT.md (S1800, PA-1) that K-sufficiency was mentioned zero times across Steps 272-278. The discrepancy is most plausibly explained by the corpus having grown further (Step 280's arrival, or a later Step 278 revision) between the two runs of the same script, rather than by a bug, since the file-count and O_core-count figures in this run are also all higher than the earlier run's.

a_rows_sample.anchor: > ## **AUTHORITATIVE STATUS: `𝒪_core` is CLOSED as a TAXONOMY and OPEN as a KERNEL.**\n> **Freezing it now would freeze an explicitly unproven minimality claim.** Step 277 says so in its own\n> boxed conclusions. **P0 "freeze canonical `𝒪_core`" must become "verify then freeze."**
a_rows_sample.statement: O_core (the operation universe) is closed as a taxonomic decomposition (Step 272A's 19-operation, 5-family O_sem) but open as a kernel/minimal primitive set, because Step 277's own conclusion explicitly states its candidate primitive transformation set T_candidate={Assert,Retract,Supersede,Merge,Split,LinkEvidence} is 'not yet proven minimal'; therefore a planned action item to freeze the canonical O_core must instead become 'verify then freeze.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **`Split`** | in `𝒯_candidate`, "minimality unresolved" | **executed: LOSSY on `ℛ`** — `Split;Merge` does not recover relations | **`Split` cannot be a state primitive without a declared `ℛ` policy.** Unreconciled. |\n| **`LinkEvidence`** | in `𝒯_candidate` | **absent** — `e` is a field of the assertion, fixed at creation | **`LinkEvidence` would MUTATE an assertion**, contradicting `ReplayAssertion`'s immutability invariant. Unreconciled. |
a_rows_sample.statement: Two unreconciled conflicts are found between Step 277's T_candidate operation set and this stream's own executed algebra: (1) executing Split followed by Merge does not recover the original relation set R (Split is lossy on R), so Split cannot be a state primitive without an explicitly declared R-handling policy; (2) LinkEvidence, if implemented as described, would mutate an existing assertion's evidence field, but in this stream's model evidence e is a field of the assertion fixed at creation time (immutable), contradicting the ReplayAssertion immutability invariant; also notes 'relate' (adding an R edge of any type) exists in this stream's algebra but is not listed separately in T_candidate, which only covers Supersede for one relation type.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | 25 | **𝒪_core** | taxonomy CLOSED / **kernel OPEN** | — | — | not executed | ✗ | `[U]` | none | **minimality unproven (see 02)** |
a_rows_sample.statement: O_core is registered as construct #25 with evidence class [U] (unresolved): taxonomy closed, kernel open, no executable test run for minimality, no real-environment observability, blocker recorded as 'minimality unproven', cross-referencing document 02 (O-CORE-AUTHORITATIVE-DETERMINATION) in the same folder.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **P0** | **Run the `𝒪_core` operation-necessity test, then freeze** | **was "freeze `𝒪_core`"** — freezing now would freeze an unproven claim |\n| **P0** | Reconcile `Split` and `LinkEvidence` against the executed algebra | **new** |
a_rows_sample.statement: Revised priority backlog: P0 item 'freeze O_core' is replaced with 'run the O_core operation-necessity test, then freeze', plus a new P0 item to reconcile Split and LinkEvidence against the executed algebra; P1 elevates deciding the EKP's real-environment witness scope (16/25 constructs have no real-environment witness) and keeps Authorize_runtime/measurement-executor work and the ND-282-1 unask recommendation (no unask; option C would void the M3 minimality proof); P2 elevates GC-1 policy-loop reconciliation (from item 8) and keeps ND-282-2 ratification (no verifier recommendation) unranked-changed; P3 book synchronization is unchanged but now explicitly ordered after GC-1 and the O_core freeze.

b_rows_sample.anchor: formal closure, computational closure, empirical closure, and governance closure are four different claims. They must never be conflated. ... No overall theory closure is claimed by Step 278.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the four-independent-closure-claims principle (formal/computational/empirical/governance) governing the whole of Step 278, and explicitly disclaims any overall theory-closure claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict = Permit | Deny | Conditional(c) | Unknown(u) ... Conditional(c)=(RequiredConditions,SatisfiedConditions,MissingConditions,ResolutionStrategy) ... WAIT ... REQUEST ... ESCALATE ... REASSESS ... BLOCK
b_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the previously vague four-value Verdict enum with a tagged union where Conditional carries a structured (RequiredConditions, SatisfiedConditions, MissingConditions, ResolutionStrategy) record, ResolutionStrategy in {WAIT, REQUEST, ESCALATE, REASSESS, BLOCK}; explicitly distinguishes Unknown (policy result undeterminable) from Conditional (policy known, conditions unresolved).

b_rows_sample.anchor: RootAuthority = ConstitutionalAuthority ... A self-rooted model is circular: Authority => Authority. An external root pushes the foundational question outside the KnowledgeOS governance model. ... A constitutional root provides an explicit meta-level
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends Constitutional Authority as the root of the authority regress (Constitution -> Authority -> Policy -> Authorization -> Operation), against three rejected alternatives (self-rooted, circular; external, pushes the question outside; organizational, unstable when organizational authority itself changes).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy as governing mechanism NOT-IN K ... but: Knowledge about Policy IN K when represented as an epistemic assertion. This resolves the ontology error.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier overstated claim (Policy not-in K) to distinguish the active governance policy (external, not itself epistemic content) from PROPOSITIONS about policy (e.g. 'policy version v became effective at t'), which are legitimate epistemic assertions and so CAN be in K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Policy | Authority | Authorization | ... Conditional | Permit | Conditional | ... Unknown | * | Unknown | This establishes deny-over-permit semantics. No positive authorization may be inferred from incomplete information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Authorization=Combine(PolicyVerdict,AuthorityVerdict) via an explicit precedence table establishing deny-over-permit semantics (any Deny or Unknown input dominates; Conditional propagates unless overridden by Deny), so no positive authorization can ever be inferred from incomplete information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 35.1 Formal Closure ... 35.2 Computational Closure ... 35.3 Empirical Closure ... 35.4 Governance Closure ... A foundation may therefore have: FC=1, CC=0, EC=0, GC=1
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces four independently-settable closure-symbol dimensions FC/CC/EC/GC (Formal/Computational/Empirical/Governance), with the explicit example that a construct can be formally-and-governance-defined (FC=1,GC=1) while not yet executable or empirically tested (CC=0,EC=0) -- FormalClosure != CompleteClosure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F1 -- Policy-free transition ... F5 -- Missing policy ... Expected: Unknown, not Permit. ... F9 -- Overlapping policy versions ... F13 -- Statistical policy boundary
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies 13 falsification tests F1-F13 (policy-free transition, authority-free transition, policy conflict, authority conflict, missing policy -> Unknown not Permit, expired policy, revoked authority under historical replay, unauthorized policy mutation, overlapping policy versions, policy rollback creating a new version, authority delegation escalation, governance propagation race, statistical policy boundary) each with a stated expected outcome, for the executable implementation in Step 279.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 278 -- FORMAL POLICY/AUTHORITY SEMANTICS: CLOSED ... COMPUTATIONAL CLOSURE: PENDING STEP 279 ... EMPIRICAL CLOSURE: PENDING STEP 280 ... GOVERNANCE CLOSURE: PENDING NORMATIVE RATIFICATION ... KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY IS NOT YET DECLARED COMPLETE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Layer 1's final HPA ruling: formal Policy/Authority semantics CLOSED, but computational closure pending Step 279, empirical closure pending Step 280, governance closure pending normative ratification (constitutional root, exact authority holder, emergency governance, policy-conflict defaults, propagation mode all listed as remaining N1-N5 normative decisions) -- no theory-completeness claim made.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The revised Step 278 is a substantially improved document. ... However, several issues remain that must be addressed before Step 278 can be considered complete. ... Step 278 is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED with required corrections.
b_rows_sample.statement: Supervisory review's overall verdict: Layer 1 correctly introduces the four closure dimensions, structured Conditional verdict, Constitutional Authority recommendation, Policy-vs-knowledge-about-policy distinction, concrete DDD contexts, and statistical/rule-independence models, but is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED pending twelve corrections.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document defines: Evaluate_pi : (K, E, C, A) -> V_pi. But it does not specify how policy rules are evaluated. ... The Combine function is underspecified ... The Statistical Measurement Model Is Not Integrated ... No Calibration Model for Probabilistic Policies
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies specific gaps in Layer 1: the policy-evaluation function's algorithm (as opposed to its signature) is unspecified; Combine's handling of Conditional-with-conditions-from-both-sides is unspecified; the statistical measurement model (P(theta>c|X)>=q) is defined but not connected to policy-rule representation or evaluation; and no calibration-verification model exists for probabilistic policy predicates (severity HIGH on the latter two).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Falsification Tests Are Not Executable ... without execution specifications, the tests are not falsifiable. ... The DDD Invariants Are Not Validated ... The Closure Matrix Is Still Too Optimistic
b_rows_sample.statement: Further identified gaps: F1-F13 lack execution specifications (setup/execute/expected/pass-criteria) so are not yet actually falsifiable; the DDD invariants G-I1..G-I5 lack enforcement-location/violation-consequence specification; and the closure matrix conflates 'Formally Specified' (definition exists) with 'Formally Closed' (definition complete and consistent) -- recommends distinguishing five closure-status labels rather than the prior binary-ish set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Policy–Authority integration model is formally specified but not yet closed. Formal Closure: CONDITIONAL -- requires corrections. ... The theory is NOT COMPLETE. ... Next: STEP 278 FINAL
b_rows_sample.statement: Supervisory ruling: Step 278 is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED, with all twelve identified issues mandatory to address before completion; directs the next artifact to be 'Step 278 Final -- Policy-Authority Integration with Corrections'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The previous Step 278 correctly identified Policy and Authority as the remaining governance dependency, but it was too strong in several places. In particular, it blurred: formal definition with computational closure; computational closure with empirical validation; governance policy with knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Accepts the supervisory review's finding that Layer 1 blurred several distinctions (formal/computational/empirical closure; governance policy vs knowledge-about-policy; authority vs authorization; policy versioning vs knowledge-state history; DDD aggregates vs mathematical objects), and states the corrected position: Policy/Authority are now a formal governance subsystem, with computational/empirical closure deferred to Steps 279/280.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C0 -- OPEN ... C1 -- FORMALLY SPECIFIED ... C2 -- COMPUTATIONALLY PARAMETRIC ... C3 -- EMPIRICALLY CLOSED ... C4 -- GOVERNANCE CLOSED ... These dimensions are ORTHOGONAL.
b_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the closure vocabulary a third time with five explicit orthogonal states C0-C4 (OPEN, FORMALLY SPECIFIED, COMPUTATIONALLY PARAMETRIC, EMPIRICALLY CLOSED, GOVERNANCE CLOSED), explicitly noting a policy can be 'formally specified + computationally executable + empirically tested + governance-open' without contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PID = Hash(content, rules, parameters, authority, validity) ... A change therefore creates a new policy identity rather than mutating the identity of an existing policy. ... Policy replacement is represented as: Supersedes(pi_18, pi_17) not deletion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines content-addressed policy-version identity (PID=Hash(content,rules,parameters,authority,validity)), so any change produces a new identity rather than mutation, with replacement represented via an explicit Supersedes relation over immutable historical policies rather than deletion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structural independence ... Inputs(r_i) intersect Inputs(r_j) = emptyset ... Logical independence ... Statistical independence ... These are different concepts. Structural independence != Logical independence != Statistical independence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines three explicitly distinct independence classes for policy rules -- structural (disjoint inputs), logical (neither entails the other), statistical (observed evaluations approximately probabilistically independent) -- correcting an earlier undifferentiated 'rule independence' concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nominal | Equality/classification | Ordinal | Ordering | Interval | Differences | Ratio | Ratios + arithmetic ... a policy must not perform x+y merely because x and y are represented numerically.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires every policy measurement to declare its measurement scale (nominal/ordinal/interval/ratio) and forbids performing an operation (e.g. addition) not licensed by that scale merely because values happen to be represented numerically; adds a calibration model (bias b=E[theta-hat]-theta, variance bound) for inexact measurement functions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Overlap without a resolution rule => INVALID. ... A node must never silently move backward ... unless an explicit historical replay operation is being performed. ... Operational policy propagation = monotonic while Replay = intentionally historical
b_rows_sample.statement: States two mandatory invariants: overlapping policy validity intervals without an explicit resolution rule are INVALID by construction (not silently resolved); and normal operational policy-version propagation must be monotonic (never silently regress to an older version) except during an explicitly intentional historical Replay.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F9 -- Unauthorized Policy Mutation ... F10 -- Historical Policy Replay ... F11 -- Overlapping Policy Conflict ... F12 -- Governance Propagation ... F13 -- Rule Independence
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds five new falsification tests F9-F13 (each with an explicit hypothesis and failure condition): unauthorized policy mutation must not activate; historical replay must use the historically-applicable policy not the current one; overlapping unprioritized policies must yield CONFLICT not a silent choice; a policy change must propagate to all nodes within its stated bound; and structurally-independent rules must not acquire hidden result-dependency through implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy, Authority in C1 ... Empirical closure requires Step 280. Governance closure requires organizational ratification. ... NEXT: STEP 279 -- POLICY AND AUTHORITY EXECUTABLE IMPLEMENTATION
b_rows_sample.statement: Final ruling: Policy and Authority are placed in closure state C1 (formally specified), with computational closure pending Step 279's executable implementation, empirical closure pending Step 280's end-to-end test, and governance closure pending organizational ratification of five listed normative decisions (ND-01 through ND-05) -- explicitly not a claim of KnowledgeOS theory completeness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Succ_{\mathcal S}(K_t,e_t) ... successor semantics must account for: newly introduced content; removed or invalidated content; persistent content; contextual applicability; provenance/history. This does not define δ as situation calculus.
a_rows_sample.statement: delta(K_t,e_t)->K_{t+1} remains an open transition problem; adopts K_{t+1}=Succ_S(K_t,e_t) as a research framework requiring successor semantics to account for five things: newly introduced content, removed/invalidated content, persistent content, contextual applicability, and provenance/history. Explicitly: this defines situation-calculus successor-state reasoning as a formal candidate to investigate delta against, not a definition of delta itself.

a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Reiter's formal ontology and axioms (already captured in S2536) under an explicit [EXT]/'extracted not endorsed' framing, emphasizing two carried-forward limitations for any KnowledgeOS transfer: the induction axiom is second-order (not fully first-order decidable), and the successor-state axiom rests on an unproven causal-completeness ASSUMPTION about the axiomatiser's own knowledge, not a theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition ... K_t -Zero-> Z_t -Lord-> L_t -Sarathi-> a_t -Commit-> e_t -delta-> K_{t+1} ... Zero, Lord, and Sarathi do not change K
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the initial Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Commit/Transition pipeline as a linear sequence culminating in a state change, with explicit invariants that Zero, Lord and Sarathi are each analytical (never transformational) and none of their outputs alone entail K_{t+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi should not 'recommend Commit'... Commitment is not an epistemic action. It is an authorization/governance action... a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t. Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Removes 'Commit' from Sarathi's action vocabulary and inserts an explicit Authorization boundary between recommendation and execution: Sarathi produces a recommendation a_t, Authorize(Knower,a_t,Policy) produces a command c_t, Execute(c_t) produces an event e_t, and only then does delta(K_t,e_t) fire -- Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition, with the missing Authorize function explicitly making the Knower's authority mathematically visible.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Execute: C -> E is too deterministic. Execution can fail... Execute(c_t) -> ExecutionResult in {Success(e),Failure(f),Partial(e,f)} ... ExecutionResult != DomainEvent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Execute from a total deterministic function C->E to one returning a structured ExecutionResult (Success/Failure/Partial), and similarly Authorize to return an AuthorizationResult (Authorized/Rejected/Deferred/Modified) rather than assuming every recommendation becomes a command; ExecutionResult is explicitly distinguished from the DomainEvent that actually triggers a transition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the epistemic cycle is actually not always a cycle... External observation -> Event -> Transition can update the state directly... Guidance is optional; Transition is fundamental. G5 - Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the closing theorem G5: Guidance (Zero/Lord/Sarathi) is not a prerequisite for every Knowledge-State transition -- a raw external observation event or a scheduled validity check can trigger delta(K_t,e_t) directly, so the lenses must never be modelled as mandatory middleware sitting between every event and the transition function; renames the pipeline from 'Epistemic Cycle' to 'Epistemic Guidance-and-Transition Cycle' to reflect this.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi \rightarrow DecisionPosture
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sarathi's output from a binary Stop/Continue decision to a richer DecisionPosture ∈ {Proceed, Investigate, ProceedWithCaveats, Defer, Escalate, UnableToDecide}, argued to be closer to Sarathi's actual role.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation \neq Assertion
a_rows_sample.statement: Strict boundary: Recommendation ≠ Assertion, Recommendation ≠ Fact, Recommendation ≠ Decision. Sārathi may say 'Investigate the moral obligation dimension' but KnowledgeOS must not silently convert that into 'Therefore Arjuna should fight' — the Knower remains the decision authority unless the domain explicitly delegates that authority. Marked as extremely important for the DDD model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Lord needs a stronger boundary too: Candidate ≠ Knowledge, Candidate ≠ Evidence, Candidate ≠ Assertion. A presentation should visually distinguish KNOWN / INFERRED / UNKNOWN / CANDIDATE / RECOMMENDED to prevent semantic contamination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(S_t) \rightarrow EpistemicFindings
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Zero's role as boundary-finder, not belief-decider: Zero(S_t) -> EpistemicFindings, Presentation ⊇ DecisionRelevant(EpistemicFindings); 'Zero does not decide what the Knower should believe. Zero says: Here is where the state has a boundary.' Also strengthens provenance: EveryDecisionRelevantClaim -> Provenance, with a worked claim-level provenance record example (Acquisition/Evidence/Observed-at/Validity/Conflict/Source).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Unknown 
eq Absent

eq NotYetInvestigated
a_rows_sample.statement: Elevates 'unknown' to a fundamental principle already implicit in Zero: Unknown ≠ Absent ≠ NotApplicable ≠ NotObserved ≠ NotYetInvestigated, illustrated by Version=UNKNOWN not meaning Version=ABSENT, and SecurityStatus=NOT_ASSESSED not meaning SecurityStatus=SAFE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq UniversalValidator
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning that Zero risks becoming a 'god object' by owning detection of gaps, conflicts, type problems, temporal problems and epistemic boundaries all at once: Zero ≠ UniversalValidator. Zero is redefined narrowly as detecting epistemic boundaries/deficiencies relevant to current state and purpose, aggregating epistemic consequences of findings from separate domain validators (schema, type, policy, security violations).

a_rows_sample.anchor: LordCandidate \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: LordCandidate ≠ Knowledge and LordCandidate ≠ Evidence: Lord can propose 'there may be a moral-obligation dimension' but it becomes knowledge only after investigation; critical to prevent AI-generated hypotheses entering the Knowledge State as facts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S\bar{a}rathiRecommendation \neq Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Sārathi needs a constitutional policy boundary: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision, SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization — Sārathi may determine the next best investigation, but the Knower decides whether to accept it unless the system has explicitly delegated authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (K,U,N,\Delta,P,Role) \rightarrow Guidance
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action as too simplistic: Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role) -> Guidance, which may then produce Decision, which may then authorize Action, giving Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action (confirming an earlier DDD warning). Also reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as three functions/lenses over the state rather than three sequential stages: Zero=Diagnose, Lord=Reason/Synthesize/Orient, Sārathi=Guide, with Decision->Action occurring outside those lenses; explicitly an architectural abstraction, not a literal theological equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (State, Norms, Role, Context, Discrepancies) \rightarrow Guidance
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action (too direct) to Sārathi:(State,Norms,Role,Context,Discrepancies)->Guidance -> CandidateActions -> Decision -> Action, giving proper separation of concerns. Reaffirms Zero as a pure DiagnosticFunction that must not itself decide ('therefore do X'). Corrects Lord from 'merely a reasoning engine/LLM reasoning' to AuthoritativeKnowledge+NormativeOrientation+InterpretiveResolution, since Krishna in the text functions as an authoritative source of teaching, not just an inference engine — called crucial for KnowledgeOS governance. Confirms Sārathi = ContextualGuidance, distinguishing Lord ('what is authoritative/true/normative') from Sārathi ('how does that apply here') from Decision ('what will I choose') from Action ('what will I actually do').

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K,I,C,P) \rightarrow \text{Epistemic Boundaries}
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as product capabilities rather than domain entities: Zero(K,I,C,P)->Epistemic Boundaries acts as an 'epistemic diagnostic engine' (missing dimensions, unknown values, missing/weak/conflicting evidence, logical contradictions, stale knowledge, contextual mismatches, unresolved questions, unsupported assumptions, Ideal-State discrepancies); Lord asks 'what else might matter?' enabling 'horizon expansion' beyond gap-checking; Sārathi:(K,I,Z,L,Q,C)->NextAction performs 'epistemic navigation', worked through a Bhīṣma-relationship example (Zero flags unknown relationship, Lord flags kinship as material, Sārathi recommends investigating it before evaluating the decision).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can we migrate this Nexus installation?
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: asked 'Can we migrate this Nexus installation?', a conventional AI answers directly, while KnowledgeOS first constructs required dimensions (version, repository inventory, blob stores, storage, network, DNS, firewall, certificates, backup, dependencies, authentication, operational constraints), runs Zero to find missing items (backup verification, firewall confirmation, certificate ownership, dependency inventory), and has Sārathi respond 'Do not decide migration readiness yet. Investigate these four items.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C) \rightarrow EvidenceCandidates
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects plain Retrieve(Query)->Documents to a goal-directed Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C)->EvidenceCandidates: the retrieval system 'knows why it is retrieving', discovering relevant dimensions (e.g. version, repository topology, blob stores, firewall, certificates for a migration decision) before retrieving. Zero can drive retrieval: given a partially-filled knowledge-state checklist, Zero reports specific gaps (backup verification, firewall rules, certificate ownership) and Sārathi generates a concrete investigation plan (search infrastructure docs for backup configuration, etc.), giving Zero -> Gap -> Sārathi -> Retrieval as part of the investigation loop, not a one-shot lookup.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
a_rows_sample.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

b_rows_sample.statement: Zero as neutral knowledge state: Zero != Nothing, it is a neutral starting condition. A new knowledge object begins without authority, evidence, validation or interpretation -- it begins as UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN is proposed as a first-class state, distinct from False and from Missing: UNKNOWN = a known, unresolved state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not force: Unknown -> False / Unknown -> Guess / Unknown -> Empty. Instead: Unknown -> Known Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Combining Zero ('unknown is a valid state') with ECS ('failure does not destroy truth, failure pauses advancement'): Unknown should be preserved and later resolved, never forced into False/Guess/Empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the elephant-and-blind-men story (cited by the source) not as 'everyone is equally right' but as 'different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object', formalized as perspectives A/B/C/D undergoing structural comparison to yield a common invariant = ZERO.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the source's citation of Subhash Kak's six-darsanas-as-cube-walls metaphor into the principle 'knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant', with the research question 'what survives when we rotate the perspective?' answered by ZERO = invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds ... The technology disappears. The invariant remains.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces modal Zero Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds, alongside a claimed prior representation Zero Z_R(K)=invariant across representations and temporal Zero Z_T(K)=invariant across time; illustrated by four possible event-bus technology choices (Kafka/RabbitMQ/sync API/another event bus) all preserving the invariant requirement 'evidence publication must remain replayable' -- the technology disappears, the invariant remains.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = ⋂_i Structure(I_i) ... What structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times, and perspectives? That may be one of our strongest candidates for robust knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as Z=intersection_i Structure(I_i) over interpretations generated from multiple world models W1..Wn (not necessarily literal set intersection in implementation), asking what structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times and perspectives, proposed as one of the strongest candidates for robust knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_i = π_i(R) ... O1 ≠ O2 doesn't necessarily mean R1 ≠ R2. It may simply mean π1 ≠ π2. This gives us a very useful projection lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the elephant analogy as a projection: observation Oi=pi_i(R) for underlying reality/object R and observer perspective pi_i, concluding that differing observations O1!=O2 need not imply differing underlying realities R1!=R2 -- it may simply reflect differing perspectives pi1!=pi2 -- named the 'projection lens'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = Invariant(O1,...,On) ... Zero is not "nothing." It is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Given observations O1..On, defines Z=Invariant(O1,...,On) and explicitly corrects a possible misreading: Zero is not 'nothing', it is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation -- called one of the strongest concepts in the entire exploration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dhātu = transformation structure ... Zero = invariant structure ... what changed? / what remained?
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AF-004 · Zero's chronology inverts CF-005's apparent ordering
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository's 'third sense' of Zero (Z-KOS-001 meta-principle) and the absence-lens sense are BOTH dated 2026-08-22; the goal-gap function sense is the LATEST (2026-08-27 era) — inverting an apparent ordering implied by CF-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-005 · Zero naming collision — a third sense
b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.

b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AF-004 · Zero's chronology inverts CF-005's apparent ordering
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository's 'third sense' of Zero (Z-KOS-001 meta-principle) and the absence-lens sense are BOTH dated 2026-08-22; the goal-gap function sense is the LATEST (2026-08-27 era) — inverting an apparent ordering implied by CF-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-005 · Zero naming collision — a third sense
b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.
